Shield AI builds trusted autonomy for national-security space missions. The Chief Engineer, Autonomy — Space Domain is the senior technical authority responsible for defining, delivering, and sustaining autonomy capabilities that convert distributed space, ground, and payload resources into timely, decision-quality data products. 

This leader owns the technical vision, system architecture, execution rigor, risk posture, verification strategy, and operational readiness of the space-autonomy solution across its lifecycle: concept development, integration, test, launch/commissioning support where applicable, on-orbit operations, software updates, and mission evolution. The role ensures that autonomy performs reliably across multi-constellation and multi-orbit mission environments, supports resilient operation in constrained or contested conditions, and delivers usable information to mission users at operational tempo. 

This is not a research position. This is a position focused on delivering mission-ready autonomy systems that perform in real-world operational environments. 

What You'll Do:

    • Serve as the senior technical authority for space-domain autonomy, accountable for mission architecture, software/system design, technical execution, product quality, technical risk, verification evidence, and customer technical confidence. 

    • Define and evolve an autonomy architecture that supports end-to-end tasking, collection, processing, exploitation, and dissemination across a heterogeneous space enterprise, including satellites, hosted payloads, ground systems, mission applications, communications networks, cloud/edge compute, and external data sources. 

    • Lead the development of automatic and autonomous behaviors for multi-constellation and/or multi-orbit tasking, including prioritization, scheduling, replanning, resource allocation, coordination, conflict resolution, and response to dynamic mission demands. 

    • Define technical approaches for autonomously selecting, cueing, configuring, and coordinating collection from all relevant payload classes, as applicable to mission needs, including but not limited to: electro-optical/infrared, AIS, SAR, RF, SIGINT, communications, environmental, navigation, or third-party/partner payload sources. 

    • Architect and govern hybrid on-board and off-board processing strategies. Establish decision criteria for where inference, data reduction, fusion, storage, prioritization, and dissemination functions execute, accounting for latency, bandwidth, compute, power, thermal constraints, availability, security, mission priority, and degraded communications. 

    • Lead the technical design of advanced exploitation capabilities, including automated triage, sensor fusion, event detection, object/activity characterization, change detection, anomaly detection, provenance, confidence estimation, and analyst-in-the-loop workflows. 

    • Own the technical approach for dissemination of mission products: data-format and interface standards, prioritization, routing, timeliness, quality metadata, access control, product traceability, downstream machine-to-machine integration, and human-user delivery. 

    • Establish coherent autonomy interfaces among spacecraft buses, payloads, avionics, flight software, communications systems, mission planning systems, ground control, cloud/edge infrastructure, data platforms, and customer mission applications. 

    • Drive technical rigor across system requirements, CONOPS, architecture descriptions, interface-control documents, trade studies, test plans, verification matrices, technical performance measures, and technical baselines. 

    • Lead autonomy technical readiness for major milestones, including concept and requirements reviews, preliminary and critical design reviews, test-readiness reviews, operational demonstrations, launch-readiness activities where applicable, commissioning, on-orbit operational assessments, and customer acceptance events.  

    • Define and execute a verification and validation strategy that combines modeling and simulation, digital engineering, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, payload/ground integration, mission rehearsal, operational test, and—in applicable programs—on-orbit validation. 

    • Identify, quantify, and retire autonomy-specific technical risks, including failure or degradation of sensors and payloads; crosslink or ground-link interruption; incomplete, delayed, conflicting, or deceptive data; resource exhaustion; model uncertainty; interface failures; cyber compromise; and unsafe or unexplainable automated action. 

    • Partner with product, program, mission operations, security, safety/mission assurance, payload, spacecraft, ground, cloud, and data-engineering leaders to balance mission performance, technical risk, cost, schedule, and customer commitments. 

    • Serve as a senior technical counterpart for government customers, mission partners, suppliers, and internal executives. Support capture, proposal technical volumes, demonstrations, mission architecture discussions, technical reviews, and customer acceptance. 

    • Build and mentor a high-performing technical organization that may include staff engineers, autonomy developers, mission planners, data/ML engineers, test engineers, and domain experts.  

Required Qualifications:

    • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, aerospace engineering, electrical/computer engineering, systems engineering, applied mathematics, robotics, physics, or a related technical discipline; advanced degree preferred. 

    • 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in autonomy, space systems, aerospace, robotics, mission systems, ISR, satellite operations, distributed systems, or comparable complex technical fields. 

    • Demonstrated experience as a Chief Engineer, Lead Systems Engineer, Technical Director, Principal/Distinguished Engineer, IPT lead, or equivalent senior technical leader responsible for end-to-end system outcomes. 

    • Significant experience designing, developing, integrating, testing, and operationalizing software-intensive mission systems with high reliability, mission assurance, or certifiability requirements. 

    • Demonstrated technical depth in several of the following: 

      • Autonomous planning, scheduling, optimization, decision-making, and multi-agent or distributed coordination. 

      • Space mission planning, spacecraft or payload operations, satellite ground systems, constellation operations, or hosted-payload architectures. 

      • Multi-orbit/multi-constellation tasking and resource management. 

      • Embedded, edge, ground, cloud, and hybrid compute architectures. 

      • On-board data processing, sensor fusion, payload control, and communication-aware autonomy. 

      • ISR, remote sensing, RF, EO/IR, SAR, communications, navigation, or other mission-payload processing and exploitation. 

      • Data-product generation, provenance, quality assessment, dissemination, APIs, and enterprise mission-data integration. 

      • Systems engineering: requirements, CONOPS, architecture, ICDs, trade studies, verification planning, technical reviews, and risk management. 

    • Experience leading a multidisciplinary, matrixed engineering organization and influencing technical outcomes across teams without requiring direct reporting control.  

    • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical trade-offs to engineers, executives, government customers, operators, and mission partners. 

    • Experience supporting customer-facing technical work, including proposals, solution architecture, test/demonstration planning, and technical reviews. 

Preferred Qualifications:

    • Experience with national security, defense, intelligence, civil-government, or commercial-space programs. 

    • Experience moving mission autonomy from prototype or research environments into sustained operational use. 

    • Demonstrated experience with operational test, mission rehearsal, launch preparation, satellite commissioning, or on-orbit anomaly response. 

    • Familiarity with safety/mission-assurance methods, cybersecurity engineering, secure software-development practices, and authorization/compliance processes relevant to space or defense systems. 

    • Experience establishing a reusable autonomy platform across multiple programs rather than delivering isolated, bespoke solutions. 

    • Active TS/SCI clearance, or established eligibility to obtain and maintain it, depending on program requirements.

jobs.title: Chief Engineer, Autonomy (R4614)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

The Chief Engineer at Shield AI is responsible for solving complex technical challenges in deploying advanced autonomy solutions on Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS).
 
As the chief authority on system architecture, design, development, risk mitigation, and product quality the Chief Engineer ensures the successful integration of Hivemind Autonomy across a range of aircraft, from small UAS to large autonomous collaborative platforms.
 
This role is part of the Hivemind Solutions organization and leads a team of engineers to deliver cutting-edge autonomous capabilities for business-to-business and defense contracts. The ideal candidate has defense industry experience as a Chief Engineer and a proven track record of leading technical teams to develop and deploy autonomous systems.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Serve as the Chief Engineer on Shield AI projects focused on developing and deploying autonomy solutions for unmanned aircraft
  • Lead a team responsible for advancing Hivemind Autonomy and shaping Department of Defense (DoD) autonomy architectures.
  • Define and assign technical objectives, make key engineering decisions, and ensure the quality and completeness of all technical deliverables
  • Provide technical leadership and oversight across both Internal Research and Development (IRAD) initiatives and DoD contracts.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS/MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical/Aerospace Engineering, and/or similar degree
  • 10+ years of industry experience in autonomy and/or UAS platforms (e.g., defense tech, self-driving car, etc.)
  • 7+ years of delivering software into production/certifiable environments with high-reliability
  • Understanding of guidance, control and navigation (GNC) (e.g. controls, estimation, planning)
  • Understanding of robotics stack (e.g., controls, estimation, perception, planning, etc.)
  • Understanding of software development processes and how to effectively deploy software
  • Experience defining technical scope and managing technical requirements, product architectures, ICDs and other system level design documentation
  • Demonstrate problem solving skills by applying a scientific technical approach
  • Customer-facing engineering leader supporting both defense and internally funded development programs
  • Contribute to government contract proposal writing
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Excellent leadership skills, driving a team of 6-20 engineers

jobs.title: Chief of Staff, AI Hive (R5599)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

As a Chief of Staff supporting functional strategy & execution, you will serve as a strategic thought partner and operational leader to an executive, helping translate business strategy into execution while improving organizational effectiveness. You will drive alignment across cross-functional teams, establish operating rhythms, coordinate strategic initiatives, and enable leaders to make faster, better-informed decisions. 
 
Operating at the intersection of strategy, business operations, communications, and program execution, you will partner closely with leaders across Finance, Engineering, Product, Operations, People, Legal, Security, IT, Facilities, and other business functions to deliver organizational priorities and drive business outcomes. 
 
This role requires a combination of strategic thinking, operational excellence, exceptional communication skills, and the ability to influence across the organization without direct authority. 

What you'll do:

  • Partner with executive leadership to translate strategic priorities into operating plans, execution roadmaps, and measurable business outcomes.  
  • Lead strategic planning processes, including the Annual Operating Plan (AOP), OKRs, business reviews, and governance rhythms to drive organizational alignment and execution.  
  • Drive complex cross-functional initiatives and day-to-day business operations, ensuring priorities remain on track, removing roadblocks, and delivering results.  
  • Act as the central coordination point across business functions, maintaining visibility into key workstreams, managing dependencies, and ensuring timely execution of strategic and operational priorities.  
  • Develop executive presentations, board materials, business communications, and reporting that support informed decision-making.  
  • Analyze business performance, operational metrics, and organizational data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and actionable recommendations.  
  • Improve organizational effectiveness by designing scalable operating mechanisms, business processes, governance frameworks, and operational workflows.  
  • Represent the executive in leadership meetings, strategic discussions, and cross-functional forums, ensuring decisions are translated into clear actions and follow-through.  
  • Build trusted relationships across the organization while exercising sound judgment, maintaining confidentiality, and acting as a force multiplier by increasing executive capacity and enabling consistent execution. 

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience. 
  • 10+ years of experience in strategy, business operations, management consulting, program management, product operations, military leadership, or a related field. 
  • Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives involving multiple executive stakeholders. 
  • Strong strategic thinking combined with excellent operational execution skills. 
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without direct authority and build alignment across diverse organizations. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing executive presentations and strategic communications. 
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities with the ability to synthesize complex information into actionable recommendations. 
  • Experience establishing executive operating rhythms, governance processes, business reviews, and planning mechanisms. 
  • Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. 
  • High degree of judgment, integrity, professionalism, and discretion when handling confidential information. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • MBA or advanced degree in Business, Engineering, Public Policy, or a related discipline. 
  • Experience supporting senior executives as a Chief of Staff, Strategic Business Partner, or Business Operations Leader. 
  • Experience working in aerospace, defense, AI, robotics, autonomous systems, or other highly technical industries. 
  • Experience in high-growth startup or scale-up environments. 
  • Familiarity with strategic planning, OKRs, portfolio management, and business operations. 
  • Experience preparing materials for executive leadership teams, boards of directors, or investors. 
  • Demonstrated success leading cross-functional transformation or organizational change initiatives. 
  • Strong financial acumen with experience supporting annual planning, budgeting, and resource allocation.

jobs.title: Configuration and Change Control Analyst (R5300)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

The Configuration and Change Control Manager is a senior individual contributor responsible for owning configuration discipline for the fielded V-BAT fleet, including aircraft, payloads, software, ground equipment, support equipment, and customer-specific configurations.This role ensures Shield AI maintains an accurate, traceable, and controlled understanding of what hardware, software, payload, and ground system configurations are deployed, which changes apply to which aircraft or customers, and how approved fixes, retrofits, releases, and service actions are controlled through execution.This position is critical to preventing configuration confusion across aircraft serial numbers, hardware revisions, software versions, payload variants, ground equipment configurations, fielded modifications, maintenance releases, and customer-specific baselines. The Configuration and Change Control Manager partners closely with Fleet Support, Sustainment Engineering, Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Customer Success, Operations, and Configuration Management to ensure changes are documented, approved, communicated, traceable, and deployed to the correct assets.The role requires strong process discipline, technical fluency, attention to detail, and the ability to drive cross-functional accountability without direct authority.

What you'll do:

  • Own and maintain the V-BAT fielded and as-maintained configuration baseline for aircraft, payloads, software, ground equipment, support equipment, and related sustainment assets.
  • Track aircraft serial numbers, hardware revisions, software versions, payload configurations, ground system configurations, fielded modifications, retrofit status, and customer-specific baselines.
  • Manage the change control process for fielded V-BAT systems, ensuring approved changes are controlled, traceable, and applied to the correct aircraft, customers, and configurations.
  • Support Engineering Change Requests, Engineering Change Orders, change impact assessments, release readiness reviews, retrofit plans, and service action planning.
  • Ensure fielded fixes, retrofits, software updates, hardware changes, payload changes, and service actions are tied to the correct serial numbers, configurations, customers, and effectivity ranges.
  • Maintain configuration records for deployed aircraft, spares, payloads, ground equipment, support equipment, and field-modified assets.
  • Partner with Fleet Support, Sustainment Engineering, Product Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Customer Success, Operations, and Configuration Management to control changes across the V-BAT fleet.
  • Support release readiness reviews for software, hardware, payload, ground system, maintenance, and support equipment updates.
  • Ensure changes are documented, approved, communicated, implemented, and traceable from engineering approval through field deployment.
  • Maintain a clear view of which customers, aircraft, payloads, ground systems, spares, and support equipment are affected by each change.
  • Define and maintain change effectivity logic, including serial number applicability, build applicability, customer applicability, configuration applicability, and retrofit applicability.
  • Coordinate with Product Engineering and Sustainment Engineering to understand technical change intent, required implementation steps, and field impact.
  • Coordinate with Fleet Support and Customer Success to ensure field teams understand which updates, inspections, retrofits, or service actions apply to each customer asset.
  • Coordinate with Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain to ensure production records, nonconformance records, part revisions, supplier changes, and field configurations remain aligned.
  • Identify configuration gaps, data inconsistencies, undocumented modifications, incomplete retrofit records, and risks to fielded fleet traceability.
  • Escalate configuration risks that could affect fleet readiness, customer support, release execution, repair decisions, or technical troubleshooting.
  • Support audits, reviews, and investigations requiring accurate configuration history, change history, serial number traceability, or fielded asset applicability.
  • Improve configuration management processes, change control mechanisms, release tracking, field modification tracking, and reporting tools as the sustainment function scales.
  • Provide leadership updates on configuration health, change control status, open risks, affected assets, and field deployment progress.

Required qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in configuration management, change control, aviation sustainment, hardware/software product support, manufacturing operations, product lifecycle management, engineering operations, or complex hardware sustainment.
  • Demonstrated experience managing configuration baselines, revision control, change effectivity, fielded asset records, engineering change processes, or product release control in a complex technical environment.
  • Strong understanding of configuration baselines, as-built records, as-maintained records, revision control, serial number traceability, effectivity management, and engineering change control.
  • Experience supporting Engineering Change Requests, Engineering Change Orders, release readiness reviews, retrofit planning, service actions, or fielded product updates.
  • Experience tracking or managing hardware revisions, software versions, payload configurations, ground equipment configurations, customer-specific configurations, or deployed asset baselines.
  • Ability to determine which aircraft, systems, customers, configurations, or serial numbers are affected by a given change, issue, release, retrofit, or service action.
  • Experience working across Product Engineering, Sustainment Engineering, Fleet Support, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Operations, Customer Success, and Configuration Management teams.
  • Strong technical fluency with bills of material, part revisions, drawings, software releases, hardware changes, configuration records, product structures, or fielded system documentation.
  • Strong process discipline and attention to detail, with the ability to maintain accurate records across multiple systems, stakeholders, and changing priorities.
  • Ability to identify configuration risks, traceability gaps, undocumented changes, incomplete records, and process breakdowns before they affect fleet readiness or customer support.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to clearly communicate change applicability, implementation status, configuration risks, and decision needs.
  • Ability to operate independently as a senior IC and drive cross-functional accountability without direct authority.
  • Ability to balance configuration rigor with field support urgency, release timelines, customer needs, and operational realities.
  • Ability to possess a Secret DoD security clearance as required by customers.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with aviation, defense, unmanned systems, robotics, aerospace manufacturing, complex hardware/software products, or deployed technical systems.
  • Familiarity with PLM, ERP, MES, CMMS, service management systems, requirements systems, software release systems, or configuration management databases.
  • Experience with aircraft serial number tracking, software release management, payload configuration management, ground system configuration, depot repair records, or field modification tracking.
  • Experience with ECO/ECR processes, MRB, FRACAS, RCCA, service bulletins, maintenance releases, retrofit campaigns, or fleet-wide service actions.
  • Familiarity with configuration audits, physical configuration audits, functional configuration audits, controlled baselines, product structures, or digital thread concepts.
  • Experience supporting military, defense, aviation, or high-reliability customer environments where configuration accuracy affects safety, readiness, supportability, or contractual commitments.
  • Experience working in a startup, high-growth, defense technology, aerospace, robotics, or advanced manufacturing environment.
  • CM2, CMII, PMP, Lean Six Sigma, APICS, aviation maintenance, systems engineering, or related certification preferred but not required.

jobs.title: Construction Design Manager (R5486)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

This role will serve as the owner's representative responsible for leading facility planning, programming, design development, and project delivery for manufacturing, engineering, laboratory, office, and secure facility projects.

This position is heavily focused on design management and will be responsible for directing external architecture and engineering (A&E) firms throughout the entire project lifecycle. The successful candidate will lead stakeholder engagement, requirements development, programming, consultant management, design reviews, constructability reviews, and technical decision-making while ensuring designs align with operational objectives, budget constraints, schedule requirements, security requirements, and long-term facility strategies.

The ideal candidate thrives in environments where requirements are evolving and can effectively guide design teams through ambiguity to produce practical, constructible, and scalable solutions. Construction oversight is expected, but the primary focus of this role is ensuring design quality, design coordination, and successful project definition before construction begins.

The initial assignment will be the planning, design, and delivery of a prototype laboratory facility supporting advanced engineering and development activities.

What you'll do:

  • Serve as the owner's lead representative for facility planning, programming, and design execution.
  • Manage and direct architecture, engineering, specialty consultant, and design-build teams.
  • Develop project requirements in partnership with engineering, manufacturing, operations, security, and executive stakeholders.
  • Convert high-level business and operational objectives into actionable facility and infrastructure requirements.
  • Lead programming efforts, space planning exercises, feasibility studies, and conceptual design development.
  • Oversee design development from concept through construction documents.
  • Establish and manage design schedules, consultant deliverables, review cycles, and design budgets.
  • Lead design review meetings and drive resolution of technical issues, scope gaps, and coordination conflicts.
  • Review architectural, civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, and specialty system designs.
  • Evaluate designs for constructability, maintainability, operational efficiency, scalability, safety, and lifecycle performance.
  • Ensure designs support manufacturing operations, engineering workflows, laboratory functions, airfield activities, and secure facility requirements.
  • Coordinate internal stakeholder reviews and ensure project requirements are properly incorporated into design documents.
  • Support permitting, entitlement, and regulatory approval efforts.
  • Provide technical leadership during procurement, contractor selection, and project execution activities.
  • Manage design-related RFIs, submittals, field modifications, and consultant support during construction.
  • Utilize AutoCAD to review, coordinate, and comment on design documentation.
  • Serve as the primary interface between internal stakeholders and external design consultants.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or related technical field.
  • Minimum 10 years of experience in design management, owner's representation, architecture, engineering, facilities development, or capital project delivery.
  • Demonstrated experience managing architecture and engineering firms on complex facility projects.
  • Strong understanding of facility planning, programming, design development, and construction documentation.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary design teams through all phases of project development.
  • Ability to review and interpret architectural and engineering drawings, specifications, calculations, and technical documentation.
  • Working knowledge of building systems, construction methods, codes, and industry best practices.
  • Proficiency with AutoCAD.
  • Experience supporting projects in active operational environments, including aviation or airfield facilities.
  • Strong stakeholder management, communication, and decision-making skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in situations with incomplete or evolving requirements.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. SECRET Security Clearance.
  • Ability to lift 50 pounds or greater and perform site visits in active construction environments.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Active U.S. SECRET Security Clearance or higher.
  • Experience supporting advanced manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or technology environments.
  • Experience planning and designing laboratories, prototype development spaces, engineering facilities, or manufacturing operations.
  • Familiarity with ICD 705 requirements and secure facility design.
  • Experience with SCIF planning, design, and accreditation processes.
  • Experience delivering projects using design-build, progressive design-build, or fast-track delivery methods.
  • Professional registration or certification such as PE, RA, PMP, CCM, LEED, or similar.
  • Experience managing mission-critical or highly technical facilities.

jobs.title: Customer Sustainment Engineer (R5502)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

Shield AI builds intelligent systems that protect service members and civilians. Our products include Hivemind autonomy software and V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and our teams support customers and operations across the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. 

Shield AI is hiring a Senior Customer Sustainment Engineer to support Hivemind systems after they reach customers and operational teams. This role sits at the intersection of customer support, systems troubleshooting, and engineering. 

Customers and forward deployed employees bring valuable operational context when they report a mission interruption, update concern, or unexpected system behavior. You will work with them to translate that context into a clear technical problem by gathering the right evidence, understanding the operating environment, narrowing the likely causes, and identifying the best path to resolution. 

Some issues will be resolved through configuration changes, deployment corrections, known workarounds, or better guidance. Others will require a product or engineering change. In either case, you will stay with the issue through resolution, keep the customer informed, and make sure the outcome is captured for future use. 

The role is the primary owner for Tier 1 support, handles a meaningful portion of Tier 2 troubleshooting, and can contribute to limited Tier 3 investigation when deeper technical experience is useful. Using DoD sustainment language, this is roughly the software equivalent of intermediate-level maintenance: resolve what can be addressed at that level, identify what needs depot-level repair, and provide engineering with a complete technical handoff. Product Support and core engineering teams provide the depot-level repair capability, while this role stays engaged to validate the result and close the loop with the customer. 

You will work closely with Forward Deployment Engineering, Product Support Engineering, Operations & Sustainment, Product, Program, Licensing, and the core Hivemind engineering teams. The goal is straightforward: help customers return to mission-ready operation while making Hivemind easier to support over time. 

What you'll do:

    • Own Tier 1 customer support and incident coordination from initial report through confirmed resolution. 

    • Gather the information needed to understand an issue, including mission impact, software version, configuration, deployment state, logs, telemetry, screenshots, network context, and reproduction steps. 

    • Troubleshoot Hivemind software, APIs, licensing and provisioning, deployments, configurations, networks, operator workflows, and partner or OEM integrations. 

    • Separate product defects from configuration problems, environmental differences, integration issues, training needs, and feature requests. 

    • Resolve common technical problems, handle appropriate Tier 2 investigations, and reproduce more complex failures in lab, simulation, or representative test environments. 

    • Recognize issues that require Tier 3 or depot-level product repair and give engineering teams concise escalation packages that explain the impact, evidence, likely causes, work already attempted, and expected result. 

    • Provide customers with clear updates, practical next steps, and technically sound workarounds while investigations are in progress. 

    • Support software releases, upgrades, onboarding, licensing and provisioning workflows, and the transition from deployment into ongoing sustainment. 

    • Turn recurring issues into troubleshooting guides, known-issue records, diagnostic tools, training material, and product feedback. 

    • Use incident patterns to identify improvements to product reliability, diagnostics, documentation, and release readiness. 

Projects you may work on:

    • Investigate a mission failure after a software update by comparing logs, configurations, versions, network behavior, telemetry, and release notes. 

    • Reproduce an autonomy, API, or integration issue and provide engineering with the evidence needed to correct it. 

    • Restore an offline customer environment affected by licensing, provisioning, time synchronization, or version compatibility. 

    • Coordinate the technical response to a high-impact customer issue and validate the workaround or fix before closure. 

    • Build a diagnostic playbook for recurring deployment, configuration, networking, or operator-workflow problems. 

Required qualifications:

    • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical, military, field-engineering, or technical experience. 

    • 7+ years of hands-on experience supporting fielded, software-enabled systems in customer, operational, test, deployment, or sustainment environments. 

    • Experience with cyber-physical, edge, mission, robotics, autonomy, aviation, defense, industrial-control, or similarly complex deployed systems. 

    • Strong troubleshooting skills across software, Linux, configuration, networking, logs, telemetry, software versions, and hardware-adjacent interfaces. 

    • A record of owning technical issues from an incomplete initial report through diagnosis and resolution. 

    • Ability to read and reason about modern C++ and use existing Python, Bash, or similar scripts during troubleshooting and log analysis. 

    • Clear written and verbal communication with customers, operators, and engineering teams, including during time-sensitive situations. 

    • Ability to write useful incident records, troubleshooting guidance, engineering escalations, and customer-facing updates. 

    • Sound judgment when working within security, export-control, safety, customer-site, contractual, and data-handling requirements. 

    • Ability to possess a Secret DoD security clearance when required by customers. 

Preferred qualifications:

    • Experience with autonomy software, robotics, unmanned systems, aviation, defense or mission software, ground-control software, SDKs, APIs, or edge-deployed systems. 

    • Experience supporting fleet operations, operational-readiness events, flight or ground test campaigns, or customer-site deployments. 

    • Familiarity with DoD sustainment, intermediate- and depot-level maintenance concepts, or comparable field-to-engineering support models. 

    • Hands-on software engineering experience writing and debugging C++ and developing Python scripts or tools for diagnostics, automation, or data analysis. 

    • Familiarity with software releases, configuration baselines, upgrade validation, rollback, and version compatibility. 

    • Experience with licensing, provisioning, offline or air-gapped environments, edge compute, time synchronization, networking, or telemetry analysis. 

    • Experience with Jira, Azure DevOps, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk, Confluence, or similar engineering and support tools. 

    • Military, operator, maintainer, field-service, mission-support, or customer-engineering experience. 

    • Active or prior security clearance. 

      •  

      Success looks like 

      After 90 days 

      • You can independently manage Tier 1 Hivemind support, resolve appropriate Tier 2 problems, and bring well-supported Tier 3 or depot-level cases to the appropriate engineering team. 

      • Customers and internal teams receive clear updates, practical next steps, and consistent follow-through. 

      • Your escalation packages allow engineering teams to begin useful work without repeating basic discovery. 

      After 6 months 

      • Common field issues have repeatable diagnostics, workarounds, and support guidance. 

      • Forward Deployment Engineers and core engineers spend less time reconstructing customer problems because the evidence and technical qualification are already in place. 

      • Incident trends are leading to improvements in Hivemind reliability, supportability, documentation, and release readiness. 

        •  
        Staff- $180,000-$270,000
        Sr Staff- $210,000-$320,000

jobs.title: Deputy Chief Engineer, X-BAT
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Job Description

Are you an experienced aircraft-development leader looking to help build a new class of autonomous combat aircraft? Are you energized by technically difficult problems, rapid execution, and the opportunity to redefine airpower? Shield AI may be the place for you.

The Deputy Chief Engineer for X-BAT will report to the Air Vehicle Lead / Chief Engineer X-BAT and serve as their primary technical deputy across the design, development, integration, test, and maturation of the X-BAT air vehicle.

This individual will help maintain the technical integrity of the aircraft while driving day-to-day engineering execution across structures, aerodynamics, propulsion, mechanical systems, avionics, electrical systems, flight controls, software, autonomy integration, manufacturing, and flight test.

The ideal candidate combines broad aircraft technical depth with strong systems thinking, sound engineering judgment, and a demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams through ambiguity. They must be comfortable moving between system-level decisions and detailed technical problem-solving while balancing performance, safety, cost, schedule, manufacturability, and mission requirements.

What You’ll Do

  • Serve as the primary technical deputy to the X-BAT Air Vehicle Lead, acting on their behalf when necessary and helping translate program objectives into clear engineering priorities.
  • Maintain the integrity of the air vehicle’s technical baseline, including system requirements, architecture, interfaces, configuration, performance, verification, and airworthiness evidence.
  • Lead the day-to-day integration of engineering activities across aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, mechanical systems, avionics, electrical systems, flight controls, software, autonomy, manufacturing, and test.
  • Drive aircraft-level technical decisions and trade studies, ensuring decisions are grounded in first-principles analysis and consider downstream effects on performance, safety, cost, schedule, producibility, maintainability, and operations.
  • Establish and maintain a disciplined technical-risk process, ensuring risks are identified early, assigned accountable owners, supported by mitigation plans, and retired through analysis or test.
  • Lead major technical and design reviews, ensuring the aircraft is sufficiently mature to progress through fabrication, ground test, flight test, qualification, and production.
  • Partner with Program Management to align technical scope with schedule, budget, staffing, supplier, and customer commitments.
  • Work closely with Manufacturing and Supply Chain to ensure designs are producible, scalable, and supported by a resilient supplier base.
  • Partner with Test and Flight Operations to define verification strategies, ground- and flight-test objectives, instrumentation requirements, test readiness criteria, and issue-resolution plans.
  • Lead rapid root-cause investigations and corrective actions for complex aircraft-level problems identified during integration, ground test, flight test, production, or operations.
  • Ensure technical decisions and engineering changes are documented, communicated, and reflected in the controlled product baseline.
  • Develop the technical leadership capabilities of engineering managers, functional leads, integrated product team leads, and senior individual contributors.
  • Communicate aircraft status, technical risks, decision recommendations, and recovery plans clearly to program leadership, executives, customers, and external partners.
  • Foster a culture of technical excellence, urgency, ownership, intellectual honesty, and constructive challenge.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 12+ years of progressive experience developing complex aircraft, military aerospace systems, autonomous aircraft, or similarly integrated aerospace products.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership on an aircraft-development program, preferably as a Chief Engineer, Deputy Chief Engineer, Air Vehicle Lead, Systems Engineering Lead, Integrated Product Team Lead, or equivalent.
  • Broad understanding of aircraft design and integration across multiple engineering disciplines, with the technical judgment to identify critical interfaces and system-level consequences.
  • Experience taking an aircraft or similarly complex aerospace system through multiple lifecycle stages, such as requirements development, preliminary and critical design, fabrication, integration, ground test, flight test, qualification, or production.
  • Experience establishing and managing system requirements, technical baselines, interface definitions, design reviews, verification plans, and engineering risks.
  • Demonstrated ability to make high-quality technical decisions with incomplete information and under aggressive program timelines.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical issues and recommendations to executive and customer audiences.
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced development environment.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, Engineering Management, or a related discipline.
  • Experience developing clean-sheet military aircraft, fighter aircraft, collaborative combat aircraft, unmanned aircraft systems, or advanced VTOL platforms.
  • Experience with propulsion integration, flight controls, vehicle management systems, autonomy integration, low-observable aircraft, or weapons and mission-systems integration.
  • Experience supporting aircraft ground test, envelope expansion, developmental flight test, airworthiness, and mishap-risk reduction.
  • Familiarity with military airworthiness frameworks, verification and validation processes, configuration management, and model-based systems engineering.
  • Experience transitioning an aircraft from rapid prototype development into qualification, rate production, and operational deployment.
  • Experience working directly with the Department of Defense, military service customers, external suppliers, and strategic industry partners.
  • Background in a high-growth aerospace organization where speed, individual ownership, and first-principles thinking were essential to program success.

The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of international defense and aerospace markets and is comfortable navigating complex government, military, acquisition, and industry stakeholder environments.   • Develop regional marketing strategies that account for differences in defense procurement processes, government structures, military organizations, acquisition timelines, budgets, and business cultures across individual markets.

  • Establish KPIs that reflect international defense sales realities, including strategic account penetration, stakeholder engagement depth, executive engagement, opportunity creation, pipeline contribution, and deal acceleration.
  • Lead regional agencies, vendors, event partners, and other external resources, ensuring high-quality execution and disciplined management of marketing investments.
  • Bring creativity, structure, cultural awareness, and adaptability to a rapidly evolving environment where new markets, capabilities, and customer opportunities are developing in real time.
  • Represent Shield AI and Field Marketing with senior internal and external stakeholders, demonstrating the credibility, judgment, and executive presence required to operate in complex aerospace and defense environments.

Job Description:

We are seeking a hands-on engineering leader to direct multiple teams spanning electrical design engineering, avionics root cause analysis, and avionics build/test operations. In this role, you will own the technical health and reliability of the avionics systems powering the V-BAT platform — leading the people, processes, and designs that take issues from field observation through root cause resolution and durable design improvement. You will operate at the intersection of design, manufacturing, quality, and fleet support, and you will be measured by the reliability, performance, and manufacturability of what your teams deliver.

What you'll do:

  • Lead and grow the team. Mentor and develop a multidisciplinary organization of electrical design engineers, root cause analysis engineers, and avionics build/test technicians, building career paths and technical depth across all three disciplines.
  • Set direction and drive execution. Establish team priorities, allocate resources against competing demands, and drive execution while fostering a culture of technical excellence, ownership, and continuous improvement.
  • Stay technical. Actively contribute to design development and reviews, hands-on root cause analysis, and the definition and validation of corrective actions — leading by technical example, not just management.
  • Own investigations end to end. Lead cross-functional failure investigations, establish and verify corrective and preventive actions, and build tooling and infrastructure that accelerate debugging, test, and issue resolution.
  • Improve system reliability. Drive coordination across Supply Chain, Reliability, Manufacturing, Quality, and Fleet Support to implement the processes and design changes that measurably increase the reliability and availability of the V-BAT system.
  • Build the standard. Establish the standards, review cadences, and metrics (e.g., reliability growth, escape rates, time-to-resolution) that make technical quality repeatable and scalable as the program grows.

Required qualifications:

  • B.S. in Electrical Engineering or an equivalent technical field.
  • 10+ years of experience, including demonstrated success leading and growing teams of electrical engineers.
  • Proven track record of building and scaling high-performing technical teams.
  • Experience working cross-functionally across design, supply chain, manufacturing, quality, and fleet/field support.
  • Proven ability to plan and execute complex electronic and electrical designs in a high-consequence industry (defense, aerospace, automotive, or medical device).
  • Demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-ownership development environment with rapidly evolving priorities.

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering.
  • Experience with structured problem-solving and failure analysis methods such as fault tree analysis, fishbone/Ishikawa diagrams, FMEA/FMECA, 8D, or similar.
  • Ownership of full product development lifecycles — from concept through release, production ramp, customer sustainment, and product retirement.
  • Experience in UAV/UAS design or other autonomous or unmanned systems.
  • Familiarity with reliability engineering practices (reliability growth modeling, MTBF/MTBUR analysis, accelerated life testing).

Leaders at Shield are expected to have strong technical fundamentals and a real history of hands-on design.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Own the technical vision, strategy, and roadmap for mechanical, thermal, and EWIS engineering across X-BAT flight and ground avionics
  • Build and scale a multi-team organization: hire and develop managers and technical leads, define org structure, and plan headcount to meet near- and long-term program goals
  • Be accountable for your organization's delivery of complex electro-mechanical hardware that survives harsh environments, from architecture through qualification and production
  • Set engineering standards, design review practices, and processes for thermal, mechanical, and harness design of flight-critical avionics
  • Serve as the final technical authority on key mechanical and thermal architecture tradeoffs, and escalate risk to program leadership with clear recommendations
  • Partner with electrical engineering, RF, PCB design, reliability, structures, supply chain, and manufacturing leaders to drive full-scope product delivery
  • Own organizational planning inputs, including resourcing, schedule commitments, supplier and contract manufacturer strategy, and make-vs-buy decisions
  • Build a culture of extreme ownership, technical rigor, and accountability
  • You won't design as an individual contributor. You must have done that work earlier in your career so you can establish what "right" looks like across the organization.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • B.S. in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering
  • 15+ years of experience in mechanical design around electronics and electrical systems, including significant early-career, hands-on design of enclosures, thermal solutions, and harness integration
  • 5+ years of people leadership, including managing managers or leading multiple engineering teams
  • Proven record of building and scaling engineering teams through rapid growth
  • Record of delivering complex avionics or electro-mechanical hardware from concept through production
  • Deep technical fluency in avionics packaging, FEA, thermal analysis, and fatigue and lifecycle testing
  • Experience setting engineering strategy, standards, and processes across an organization
  • Experience managing relationships with fabrication shops, contract manufacturers, and key suppliers
  • Ability to operate in a fast-paced, agile environment with shifting priorities
  • A demonstrated record of working hard, being trustworthy, holding yourself to high standards, and being kind to others
  • Ability to obtain a Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Background in high-rate hardware production, such as satellites, EV power electronics, or autonomous vehicles
  • Experience with DO-160, MIL-STD-810, or similar environmental qualification standards
  • Degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or equivalent Engineering

Job Description: 


Shield AI is building the world’s best AI pilot to protect service members and civilians with intelligent systems. As we scale both our proven VBAT platform and develop next-generation systems like XBAT, we are investing in how we build—not just what we build. 

We are seeking a senior technical leader to define and operationalize engineering design standards across the company. This position is focused on establishing engineering excellence—driving consistency, rigor, and scalability across design, analysis, certification, CAD, documentation, and configuration management.

jobs.title: Director, International Growth Campaign Leader (R5851)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

The Director, International Growth Campaign Leader leads the internal operating system behind Shield AI international X-BAT pursuits. Regional, country and opportunity-focused Go-To-Market (GTM) leaders own their customers, their regional and in-country strategies, and their individual captures. This role owns the layer above them: the single, integrated view across regions, and the mechanisms that turn that view into faster decisions, earlier risk mitigation, and better-supported GTM leads. 

Each GTM lead sees their own campaign clearly. No one else sees the whole international board. This role does. It connects individual pursuits to shared dependencies — U.S. Government approvals, foreign disclosure and export sequencing, engineering and product capacity, aircraft and test availability, indirect investment, partner and industrial strategy — and makes sure competing regional timelines and strategies are sequenced deliberately rather than reactively. 

This is a pre-award enablement and integration role. It is explicitly not the primary customer interface, and it does not extend to the execution of customer-funded programs after award, though it may involve developing projections to better inform execution-supporting decision making. The GTM lead remains the face to the customer, the owner of the account plan, and the accountable capture lead for their country. This role makes those leads faster, better armed, and better supported. 

What you'll do:

  • Own the global view. Build and maintain the integrated international campaign picture across all X-BAT regional and country pursuits: strategy status, critical path, milestones, dependencies, decision points, and campaign health in one authoritative picture. 
  • Enable the GTM leads. Give regional and country GTM leads the templates, playbooks, data, competitive inputs, cost and schedule inputs, and cross-functional access they need to build and execute their capture plan. Your success is measured by their outcomes. 
  • Synchronize across company functions. Ensure engineering, product, export, legal, contracts, finance, government relations, and business operations have common understanding of a single prioritized international campaign plan, so GTM leads are not individually negotiating for the same scarce resources. 
  • Map the U.S. Government and approval critical path. Maintain the enterprise view of FMS, DCS, and hybrid pathway dependencies — foreign disclosure, exportability, releasability, technology security, and interagency approval sequencing — and translate them into country-level timeline implications the GTM leads can act on. Government Relations and the relevant functional owners lead those engagements; this role ensures they are planned early, sequenced correctly, and never discovered late. Understand and communicate the global GTM projections in ways that support enabling functions’ ability to anticipate and properly resource for future demand. 
  • Surface conflicts between campaigns. Identify where two or more regional campaigns compete for the same aircraft, test window, engineering effort, approval bandwidth, or indirect dollar, and bring executive leadership a clear tradeoff and a recommendation. 
  • Drive executive decision quality. Run the operating cadence — campaign reviews, gate reviews, risk registers, action tracking, and executive dashboards — so leadership receives timely, accurate, decision-ready information on overall international capture health in support of resource allocation. Steward indirect investment. Work with Finance and Business Operations to track campaign investment, indirect spend, and resource planning against campaign priorities and expected return. 
  • Scale the discipline. Capture lessons learned across international efforts and convert them into repeatable tools, templates, metrics, and playbooks so each new campaign starts further ahead than the last. 
  • Support a culture of accountability, urgency, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 

Decision rights and interfaces:

    This role is accountable for: the integrated international campaign plan; the operating cadence and campaign-health reporting; identification and escalation of cross-campaign dependencies, conflicts, and risks; the consolidated U.S. Government approval and disclosure roadmap; and recommendations on investment prioritization and sequencing. 

    Regional, country and opportunity GTM leads are accountable for: customer relationships and engagement, in-country strategy, partner and industrial development, win strategy and price-to-win for their pursuit, proposal content, and the bid/no-bid recommendation for their opportunity. 

    Government Relations, Export, Legal, and Contracts are accountable for: interagency and embassy engagement, export authorizations, disclosure determinations, legal positions, and contracting terms. 

    Engineering and Product are accountable for: technical solution definition, configuration decisions, and performance commitments. 

    Strategy and Operations is responsible for enterprise, cross-product strategy, of which the products this role directly supports would be a part. Program Management is accountable for: execution of customer-funded programs after award. 
     
    This role will be complemented by a parallel position whose focus will be on integration across all U.S. customers, and with whom close collaboration will be required.  

    External customer engagement by this role is in support of, and at the invitation of, the responsible GTM lead. 

Required qualifications:

  • 12+ years in international B2G capture management, program management, strategic operations, business operations, technical program management, or a comparable cross-functional leadership role.  
  • Demonstrated success leading highly complex initiatives with multiple interdependent workstreams across engineering, business development, operations, finance, and executive leadership. 
  • Working knowledge of international defense pursuit dependencies, including FMS, DCS, or hybrid acquisition pathways and the approval, disclosure, and exportability sequencing that governs them. 
  • Proven ability to influence without direct authority and to drive accountability across functions and geographies. 
  • Strong executive communication: leadership briefings, dashboards, metrics, and decision-support materials that lead to decisions rather than discussion. 
  • Deep operational rigor in integrated schedules, critical path, milestones, action tracking, dependency management, and risk mitigation. 
  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-changing environments with competing priorities across multiple time zones. 
  • A service orientation toward the functional roles this position supports, and the judgment to know when to escalate versus resolve quietly. 
  • Demonstrated alignment with Shield AI core values: Do What Honor Dictates, Live as a Servant Leader, Pursue Excellence. 
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required, and to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience supporting Department of War, aerospace, autonomy, robotics, aviation, or defense-technology organizations.  
  • Experience within B2G business development, capture, proposal operations, strategic planning, or growth organizations running multiple concurrent international pursuits. 
  • Familiarity with U.S. Government international engagement mechanisms such as foreign disclosure processes, security cooperation planning, embassy and country team coordination, or interagency advocacy. 
  • Experience building executive dashboards, KPIs, operational scorecards, or portfolio health metrics. 
  • Experience supporting executive staff, chief-of-staff organizations, Strategy and Operations teams, or enterprise PMOs. 
  • Experience with tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Jira, Confluence, or The AI Work Platform for People & Agents | monday.com . 
  • MBA or advanced degree; PMP, Agile, or Lean Six Sigma certification. 

Success in this role:

  • Every regional campaign has an approved strategy, a critical-path schedule, and a mapped approval pathway that the GTM lead owns and uses. 
  • GTM leads report that the role makes their campaigns easier to run, not heavier to report on. 
  • U.S. Government, export, and disclosure dependencies are identified early enough to change the outcome rather than explain it. 
  • Cross-campaign resource and timing conflicts reach leadership early enough for meaningful action, and as a decision with a recommendation. 
  • Executive leadership can see, at any time, an accurate health picture of the international X-BAT portfolio and make investment calls with confidence. 
  • Campaign mechanisms are reused across countries, and each new pursuit stands up measurably faster than the previous one.

jobs.title: Director, Mission Systems
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Job Description
Are you a mission-driven engineering leader passionate about developing advanced autonomous aircraft? Do you want to help deliver capabilities that provide decisive advantage in contested environments? Shield AI may be the place for you.
 
Shield AI is seeking a Director of Mission Systems to lead multidisciplinary teams spanning operational analysis, aircraft survivability, communications, and integrated mission systems for our next-generation autonomous aircraft. This leader will establish the organization’s technical and business strategy, align investments and priorities with product and program objectives, and oversee execution from early concept development through integration, flight test, and fielding.
 
The ideal candidate has led a multidisciplinary organization supporting complex military aircraft or autonomous systems and brings strong business acumen alongside sound technical judgment. This individual need not be a subject-matter expert in every discipline but must understand how operational analysis, survivability, communications, payloads, avionics, autonomy, and weapons integration combine to drive mission effectiveness.
 
What You’ll Do
  • Lead and develop a multidisciplinary organization spanning operational analysis, survivability, communications, and integrated mission systems.
  • Establish clear priorities, accountability, organizational objectives, and operating rhythms that enable teams to execute effectively.
    Define technical strategy, capability roadmaps, and investment priorities aligned with aircraft program objectives, customer requirements, and broader business goals.
  • Oversee the development of integrated mission-system architectures encompassing sensors, payloads, avionics, weapons, secure communications, autonomy, and aircraft survivability.
  • Direct modeling, simulation, wargaming, and system-of-systems analysis to evaluate mission effectiveness, operational performance, emerging threats, and aircraft design alternatives.
  • Lead cross-functional trade studies that balance mission capability, survivability, technical risk, cost, schedule, manufacturability, and program maturity.
  • Ensure disciplined execution from requirements definition and architecture development through hardware-in-the-loop testing, signature validation, flight test, certification, and fielding.
  • Partner with engineering, product, program management, business development, and aircraft leadership to deliver integrated and mission-relevant capabilities.
  • Engage DoD customers, operators, suppliers, and government stakeholders to shape requirements, refine concepts of operations, support key decisions, and communicate the operational value of Shield AI’s solutions.
  • Recruit, coach, and develop people managers and senior technical leaders while building organizational depth and succession capability.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable system-safety, airworthiness, cybersecurity, security, and certification requirements.
 
Required Qualifications
 
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, mathematics, or another relevant technical discipline.
  • 10+ years of experience supporting complex military aircraft, autonomous systems, or other aerospace and defense programs.
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing a multidisciplinary engineering organization that includes people managers and senior technical leaders.
  • Broad working knowledge across multiple relevant disciplines, including mission systems, operational analysis, modeling and simulation, survivability, secure communications, avionics, sensors, payloads, or weapons integration.
  • Experience establishing organizational and technical strategies while managing technical, programmatic, and organizational risk.
  • Proven ability to balance mission performance and engineering requirements with cost, schedule, product maturity, and business priorities.
  • Experience overseeing complex aircraft capabilities across the product lifecycle—from requirements and architecture through integration, test, certification, fielding, and sustainment.
  • Executive-level communication skills with demonstrated success influencing customers, operators, business leaders, engineering teams, and government stakeholders.
    U.S. citizenship with an active Secret security clearance and the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret clearance and required SAP/SAR accesses.
 
Preferred Qualifications
  • Master’s degree or PhD in aerospace engineering, systems engineering, electrical engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Leadership experience on military UAS, advanced autonomous aircraft, collaborative combat aircraft, or fifth-generation fighter programs involving integrated mission systems and survivability.
  • Demonstrated success advancing a product or major capability from customer shaping and early concept development through acquisition, integration, flight test, validation, and tactical deployment.
  • Experience overseeing multi-domain operational analysis, CONOPS development, force-on-force modeling, threat assessment, or survivability analysis in contested environments.
  • Working knowledge of model-based systems engineering and SysML, DoD acquisition and JCIDS processes, electronic warfare, low-observable communications, and AI-enabled sensors or payloads.
  • Experience developing modular, open-system mission architectures that support rapid capability insertion and third-party payload integration.
  • Active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility and experience supporting classified DoD or Intelligence Community programs.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Job Description:

As the Director of SOX Compliance, you will build, lead, and continuously improve the company's Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance program in support of a high-growth, public-company environment. Reporting to the Corporate Controller (or Chief Accounting Officer), you will partner closely with Finance, Internal Audit, IT, Engineering, HR, Legal, and business leaders to ensure an effective internal control environment while enabling business growth.

This is initially an individual contributor leadership role (Radford P6) with significant cross-functional influence and executive visibility. As the organization grows, this role is expected to evolve into a people management position with responsibility for building and leading a SOX compliance team.

What you'll do:

  • Own and lead the company's end-to-end SOX 404 compliance program, including business process, entity-level, and IT general controls (ITGCs).
  • Develop and maintain the annual SOX strategy, risk assessment, scoping, testing plan, and compliance calendar.
  • Partner with control owners to document, assess, and improve key business processes and internal controls.
  • Coordinate management's annual SOX assessment and support external audit requirements to ensure timely completion.
  • Evaluate control deficiencies, facilitate root cause analysis, and drive remediation efforts through successful closure.
  • Monitor regulatory developments and evolving best practices to continuously enhance the SOX program.
  • Collaborate with Finance Transformation, ERP, and business system implementation teams to ensure appropriate controls are designed into new processes and technologies.
  • Drive automation and continuous monitoring opportunities to improve efficiency and control effectiveness.
  • Develop executive-level reporting and present SOX program status, risks, and remediation progress to senior leadership and Audit Committee stakeholders.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to business leaders on internal controls, governance, and risk management.
  • Establish and maintain SOX policies, methodologies, documentation standards, and training programs.
  • Support broader internal control, governance, and enterprise risk initiatives as needed.
  • Help define the future organizational structure of the SOX function, including recruiting, mentoring, and developing team members as the program expands.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
  • CPA, CIA, or equivalent professional certification.
  • 15+ years of progressive experience in SOX compliance, internal audit, external audit, accounting, or internal controls.
  • Experience leading SOX programs for publicly traded companies or organizations preparing for public company readiness.
  • Strong knowledge of SOX 404 requirements, COSO Internal Control Framework, and SEC reporting environment.
  • Experience with business process controls, entity-level controls, and IT general controls.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Experience managing external auditors and coordinating complex compliance activities across multiple functions.
  • Excellent project management, analytical, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting to executive leadership.
  • Proven ability to identify process improvement opportunities while maintaining a strong control environment.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in aerospace, defense, manufacturing, hardware, or other complex operational environments.
  • Experience supporting ERP implementations or major systems transformations (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Workday, etc.).
  • Experience with GRC platforms such as AuditBoard, Workiva, Archer, ServiceNow GRC, or similar technologies.
  • Experience leading SOX readiness for IPOs or scaling public-company compliance programs.
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity controls, automated controls, and emerging technologies supporting compliance.
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or process improvement experience.
  • Demonstrated success building or scaling compliance organizations.
  • Passion for mentoring and developing talent, with an interest in growing into a formal people leadership role as the organization expands.

Job Description:

As a Hivemind Solutions Flight Test Director (ACP Programs), you will serve as the end-to-end technical leader responsible for the integration, verification, and operational test of Hivemind AI Pilot capabilities on portfolio of group 5 UAS/Autonomous Collaborative Platforms (ACP).

You will own the strategy, planning and execution of complex, multi-phase test campaigns supporting the transition of autonomy capabilities from simulation and lab environments to full-scale flight test and operationally relevant mission scenarios, including multi-vehicle coordination. Using a disciplined fly–fix–fly methodology, you will drive rapid capability maturation while maintaining rigorous safety, configuration control, and mission assurance standards. 

This role will serve as the single technical authority for test execution across the portfolio of ACP efforts, responsible for managing risk, test readiness and driving test execution  Here, you will serve as primary focal to facilitate coordination across OEM partners, government customers and internal functional teams rs to deliver high-impact autonomy capabilities at scale.

What you'll do:

  • Act as Test Director and technical lead for integration and flight test of Hivemind autonomy on group 5 ACP systems, including multi-aircraft coordination scenarios in LVC and empirical flight test scenarios.
  • Own test strategy and execution across the full development lifecycle, including system-level verification & validation, test phasing, and prioritization across SIL, HIL, simulation, ground, and flight test environments
  • Plan and execute large-scale flight test campaigns, including complex mission scenarios involving cooperative autonomy, human-machine teaming, and distributed systems
  • Serve as the final authority during mission autonomy test operations, directing test conduct and approving test plans, procedures, and execution flow
  • Coordinate cross-functional execution across software, hardware, systems engineering, flight operations, safety, and program leadership teams
  • Define mission-level performance metrics and success criteria, ensuring traceability from requirements to test outcomes and operational effectiveness
  • Own test infrastructure strategy, including large-scale simulation environments, SIL/HIL systems, aircraft integration labs, and flight test assets
  • Lead on-aircraft integration and flight test operations with platform OEM partners, including system configuration, software deployment, real-time troubleshooting, and post-flight data analysis
  • Serve as primary coordinator working with platform OEMs to define and enforce test readiness criteria (entry/exit), define safety-of-flight and mission risk management, airspace coordination and test hazard identification, analysis, and mitigation to ultimately make go/no-go decisions for progression into ground and flight test events
  • Establish and scale test processes, standards, and best practices aligned with DoD DT&E/OT&E expectations and operational test rigor

  • Strong background in full-scale aviation test environments, including aircraft integration, ground test, and flight operations
  • Experience with system-level verification & validation across multiple test environments (SIL, HIL, simulation, and flight)
  • Proven ability to plan and execute complex, multi-phase flight test campaigns involving multiple stakeholders and dependencies
  • Experience working cross-functionally across software, hardware, avionics, systems engineering, safety, and program teams
  • Strong understanding of safety-of-flight principles, risk management, and disciplined test execution in aviation environments
  • Proficiency in Python or similar tools for test automation, data analysis, or system validation
  • Excellent technical leadership and communication skills, including briefing to senior leadership and external customers
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a SECRET clearance; U.S. citizenship required

  • Experience supporting Autonomous Collaborative Platforms (ACP), loyal wingman concepts, or multi-vehicle autonomous systems
  • Prior role as Flight Test Director, Test Conductor, or Lead Flight Test Engineer on full-scale aircraft programs
  • Familiarity with military aviation test processes, including DT&E and OT&E frameworks
  • Experience operating in or supporting government flight test ranges and operational environments
  • Background in autonomy, AI/ML-enabled systems, or human-machine teaming in aviation contexts
  • Experience with airworthiness processes, flight clearance, and configuration control for aircraft systems
