jobs.descriptionHtml:
Opening from US - X-BAT with ITAR exposure, S/SAR Clearance
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

    About Shield AI

    Shield AI develops AI-powered autonomy software and aircraft systems that protect service members and civilians by enabling intelligent operations in contested environments. As part of the X-BAT program, you will help develop and validate next-generation autonomous aircraft and mission-critical hardware that must perform reliably in demanding operational conditions.

    Job Description:

    Shield AI is seeking a Software Engineering Manager to lead the X-BAT Hardware Test Software team. This team builds and sustains automated production test stands used to functionally test avionics and aircraft electrical assemblies.

    You will lead software engineers developing test frameworks, station-control software, equipment interfaces, data collection, and automated pass/fail evaluation. Our systems interact with custom fixtures, instrumentation, embedded devices, FPGA-enabled hardware, and avionics units under test.

    The ideal candidate has managed engineering teams and has personally built or led the development of automated hardware test systems used in production, manufacturing, qualification, or other high-consequence environments. You know what robust test automation looks like: safe operation, repeatable results, useful diagnostics, configuration control, traceability, maintainability, and a practical path from prototype to sustained production use.

What You'll do:

  • Lead, mentor, and grow a team of software engineers supporting X-BAT avionics production test.

  • Own the technical roadmap and execution for automated test stands, reusable test frameworks, station software, and test-data systems.

  • Build scalable Python-based software for test sequencing, instrument and fixture control, unit-under-test communication, measurement collection, pass/fail evaluation, and reporting.

  • Guide software architecture, code quality, configuration management, CI/CD, release processes, documentation, and operational support.

  • Partner closely with electrical engineers to translate avionics interfaces, functional requirements, and failure modes into automated test coverage.

  • Partner with mechanical engineers to ensure fixtures, cabling, connectors, serviceability, safety, and operator workflows support reliable production testing.

  • Work with FPGA and embedded-software teams to configure, communicate with, and validate FPGA-enabled avionics hardware.

  • Improve test coverage, station uptime, throughput, failure triage, test repeatability, and traceability.

  • Establish metrics and processes for regression health, station reliability, first-pass yield, retest rate, false failures, and recurring failure modes.

  • Support root-cause analysis across the unit under test, fixture, instrumentation, test software, embedded software, FPGA behavior, and electrical interfaces.

Required Qualifications:

    • 5+ years of experience in software engineering, test automation, embedded systems, hardware-integrated software, manufacturing test, avionics, aerospace, robotics, automotive, industrial systems, or similar fields.

    • 2+ years of direct people-management experience leading software, test, or hardware-integration engineers.

    • Demonstrated experience building, deploying, and sustaining automated functional-test systems for complex hardware.

    • Strong Python experience, particularly for automation frameworks, hardware communication, instrument control, data acquisition, and test orchestration.

    • Experience with C++ or C in embedded, systems, device-control, or hardware-facing applications.

    • Experience working directly with electrical hardware, test fixtures, instrumentation, and devices under test.

    • Familiarity with FPGA-enabled hardware and the ability to work effectively with FPGA engineers on system-level test and debug.

    • Familiarity with common interfaces and protocols such as Ethernet, TCP/IP, UDP, serial, CAN, SPI, I2C, USB, GPIO, PCIe, or JTAG.

    • Experience with Git, code review, automated testing, CI/CD, release management, and configuration control.

    • Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively across software, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, and program teams.

Preferred Qualifications:

    • Experience developing automated production test equipment for avionics, aerospace, defense, autonomous systems, robotics, or other mission-critical hardware.

    • Experience designing reusable test frameworks rather than only writing one-off test scripts.

    • Experience with programmable power supplies, electronic loads,, DAQ systems, digital I/O, network equipment, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or custom test fixtures.

    • Experience with FPGA programming, bitstream management, register-level control, JTAG, board bring-up, or FPGA-adjacent debug.

    • Experience with embedded Linux, microcontrollers, board-support packages, device drivers, or real-time systems.

    • Experience with production traceability, serial-number tracking, test-result databases, calibration workflows, manufacturing systems, or quality systems.

    • Experience in a regulated, safety-critical, mission-critical, or configuration-controlled engineering environment.

Job Description:

Shield AI is hiring a Lead Financial Analyst, Aircraft Business Unit to support financial planning, forecasting, and decision support for the Aircraft Business Unit. This role emphasizes business partnering, forecasting, variance analysis, and translating operational drivers into actionable insights.

What you'll do:

    Support forecasting and planning for the Aircraft Business

  • Lead monthly forecasting, quarterly outlooks, and annual planning for assigned Aircraft Business departments and programs.
  • Build and maintain financial models that connect headcount, labor, material, overhead, and operating initiatives to business performance.
  • Analyze actuals versus plan, identify risks and opportunities, and provide clear recommendations to business leaders.
  • Translate production, engineering, and program assumptions into financial impacts for spend, margins, and resource needs.
  • Prepare reporting packages and presentations for finance leadership and Aircraft Business reviews.

    • Partner with Aircraft Business leaders

  • Serve as the Finance Business Partner to leaders across engineering, operations, supply chain, manufacturing, and program management within the Aircraft Business.
  • Support decision-making on hiring, labor planning, vendor spend, capital investments, and operating tradeoffs.
  • Partner with program and functional leaders to improve forecast accuracy, cost visibility, and accountability.
  • Provide ad hoc analysis on key business questions, including rate, volume, mix, productivity, and cost reduction opportunities.

    • Improve reporting and planning processes

  • Build repeatable reporting, dashboards, and planning templates that reduce manual work and improve insight quality.
  • Partner with Corporate FP&A, Accounting, HR, and business systems teams to improve data quality and planning inputs.
  • Support enhancements to planning tools and financial systems, including Anaplan models, reporting workflows, and source-system integration needs.
  • Document business requirements clearly and translate finance needs for technical teams.

Required qualifications:

  • 7+ years of experience in FP&A, program finance, operations finance, or business finance.
  • Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and variance analysis skills.
  • Experience partnering with operational or technical teams to support planning and decision-making.
  • Ability to connect operational drivers to financial outcomes in a complex, fast-paced environment.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to present insights clearly to cross-functional leaders.
  • Advanced Excel and proficiency with planning or ERP systems; experience with Anaplan is a plus.
  • Comfortable operating with ambiguity and managing multiple priorities at once.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in aerospace, defense, or other complex manufacturing environments.
  • Familiarity with manufacturing finance, program finance, inventory or cost accounting, and capital planning.
  • Experience supporting engineering, operations, supply chain, or production organizations.
  • Exposure to government contract structures, program reviews, or defense-related reporting rhythms.
  • Strong data fluency, including dashboards, data models, and system-driven planning processes.

Job Description:

Join a high-impact quality engineering team supporting the development and production of next-generation autonomous systems. This role is focused on dimensional analysis, metrology strategy, and inspection planning to ensure hardware meets critical design and manufacturing requirements. You will work closely with design, manufacturing, supplier quality, and production teams to develop scalable inspection methodologies that improve product quality, repeatability, and manufacturing confidence.

We are seeking a Metrology Engineer with experience in dimensional inspection, GD&T interpretation, measurement system analysis, and metrology process development within aerospace, defense, robotics, or precision manufacturing environments.

What you'll do:

  • Develop and execute dimensional inspection strategies for complex mechanical assemblies and precision components
  • Perform dimensional analysis and measurement studies to validate design intent, manufacturing capability, and assembly fit
  • Define metrology processes, tooling, and inspection methods using CMMs, laser trackers, scanners, and other precision measurement systems
  • Partner with design and manufacturing teams to improve tolerance schemes, GD&T application, and inspection efficiency
  • Support root cause investigations related to dimensional nonconformance, assembly variation, and manufacturing defects
  • Analyze measurement and process capability data to improve repeatability, product quality, and production readiness

Required qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in metrology, dimensional engineering, manufacturing quality, or precision inspection environments
  • Strong understanding of GD&T, tolerance analysis, datum structures, and dimensional validation methods
  • Experience programming or operating metrology equipment such as CMMs, laser trackers, structured light scanners, or portable measurement systems
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, CAD models, and manufacturing documentation for complex assemblies
  • Experience developing inspection plans, measurement strategies, and process capability studies in production environments
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to communicate technical findings across cross-functional teams

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience supporting aerospace, defense, robotics, or autonomous systems programs
  • Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001, and regulated manufacturing environments
  • Experience with NX, PolyWorks, PC-DMIS, SpatialAnalyzer, or similar metrology and dimensional analysis software
  • Experience supporting first article inspections (FAI), production qualification, or supplier quality initiatives

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

We are seeking an experienced Staff Product Support to support the design, development, integration, and fielding of a next-generation autonomous aircraft system. This role will lead the logistics planning, supply support, sustainment analysis, and lifecycle support activities across development, flight test, production, and operational sustainment.

The ideal candidate has strong experience supporting military or defense aviation programs and understands how logistics products, supportability analysis, maintenance planning, and supply chain execution contribute to mission availability and operational readiness. This position requires hands-on experience with Maintenance Task Analysis, Logistics Control Numbers, Reliability and Maintainability artifacts, and Supply Support planning and execution.

What you'll do:

  • Lead logistics and sustainment planning activities for a UAS program across design, production, deployment, and field support phases.
  • Develop, manage, and maintain integrated logistics support products, including maintenance concepts, support equipment design, provisioning inputs, spares planning, and sustainment documentation.
  • Perform and manage Maintenance Task Analysis to define preventive and corrective maintenance requirements, task frequencies, required tools, support equipment, skill levels, labor hours, and maintenance levels.
  • Develop and maintain Logistics Control Number structures to support provisioning, maintenance planning, technical documentation, configuration tracking, and sustainment data management.
  • Partner with engineering, program management, manufacturing, supply chain, field operations, and customer stakeholders to ensure logistics requirements are incorporated into system design and program execution.
  • Support Reliability and Maintainability activities, including Level of Repair Analysis, FMECA data analysis, maintainability assessments, corrective action planning, reliability growth inputs, and operational availability improvement initiatives.
  • Lead supply support activities, including spares analysis, provisioning, parts forecasting, inventory planning, reorder recommendations, repair pipeline coordination, sustainment risk identification, and obsolescence management.
  • Coordinate with suppliers, depots, repair vendors, and internal teams to ensure timely availability of parts, support equipment, and logistics resources.
  • Support proposal development, basis of estimate inputs, staffing plans, sustainment strategies, and logistics cost estimates for new and existing UAS programs.
  • Ensure logistics activities comply with applicable defense standards, contract requirements, export control requirements, and company processes.

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in logistics, engineering, supply chain, aviation maintenance, business, or a related field; equivalent military or defense logistics experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
  • 8+ years of experience supporting UAS or fighter aircraft logistics and sustainment
  • Demonstrated experience with Maintenance Task Analysis and development of maintenance planning data.
  • Expertise of Logistics Control Number structures and their use in provisioning, maintenance planning, and supportability analysis.
  • Experience with Reliability and Maintainability principles, including failure modes, maintainability drivers, reliability growth, availability metrics, and field performance analysis, and LORA development
  • Hands-on supply support experience, including spares planning, provisioning, inventory management, parts forecasting, repairables management, and sustainment execution.
  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings, bills of material, configuration data, maintenance data, and technical documentation.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with engineering, program management, supply chain, manufacturing, quality, field service, and customer teams.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and organizational skills with the ability to lead logistics efforts in a fast-paced program environment.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Proven experience with integrated product support elements, including product support management, supply support, support equipment, manpower and personnel, facilities, maintenance planning,
  • Experience with provisioning, sparing, or supportability tools such as PowerLOG-J, SLICwave, COMPASS, CASA, OPUS10, EAGLE, or similar systems.
  • Knowledge of MIL-STD-1388 legacy logistics concepts, GEIA-STD-0007, SAE TA-STD-0017, MIL-HDBK-502A, or related product support standards.
  • Experience developing logistics inputs for CDRLs, technical manuals, maintenance plans, provisioning data, sparing recommendations, or lifecycle sustainment plans.
  • Experience with ERP, PLM, or MRP systems such as SAP, Oracle, Costpoint, Teamcenter, Arena, Windchill, or similar platforms.
  • Active and current security clearance with ability to obtain SAP

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:
Shield AI is seeking a highly capable Production Supervisor to lead a team of avionics and electrical assembly technicians, integration, functional testing, and troubleshooting for advanced autonomous aircraft development programs. This leadership role is responsible for building the people, processes, and disciplined production environments required to support rapid prototype development, new product introduction, and the transition from early builds to flight‑ready hardware. 
The ideal candidate blends strong hands‑on technical expertise with operational leadership, thrives in fast‑paced manufacturing settings, and has experience developing high‑performing technician teams from the ground up. You will work cross‑functionally with Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, and Production Planning to ensure material readiness, tooling, documentation, and test equipment are in place, while driving schedule performance, configuration‑management compliance, and continuous improvement across production operation.

What you'll do:

  • Lead technicians performing avionics and electrical assembly, installation, integration, functional testing, troubleshooting, rework, inspection support, and production or flight‑readiness activities.
  • Oversee work assignment, workload prioritization, coaching, mentoring, training, performance feedback, cross‑training, policy enforcement, and development of daily and weekly operating plans.
  • Maintain control of manufacturing and integration environments, ensuring strict adherence to safety, workmanship standards, ESD/FOD prevention, calibration, tool control, serialized hardware traceability, nonconformance processes, quality requirements, and configuration‑management compliance.
  • Demonstrate proficiency with electrical and avionics test equipment and guide disciplined troubleshooting and root‑cause analysis across electrical, electronic, wiring, sensor, power, and data‑interface systems.
  • Read, interpret, and apply harness and PCBA schematics, wiring diagrams, engineering drawings, interface‑control documents, bills of material, work instructions, travelers, test procedures, and other configuration‑controlled documentation.
  • Use production and test data—including yield, defects, failures, rework, labor utilization, WIP, material availability, schedule performance, and training coverage—to identify risks, make sound operational decisions, drive continuous improvement, and escalate issues appropriately.
  • Lead production-readiness execution for prototype, developmental, pre-production, and first-article VBAT hardware/software from engineering release through flight-ready delivery.
  • Develop and manage prototype and pre-production build schedules, production-floor cut-ins, readiness milestones, risks, dependencies, and recovery plans.
  • Support first-article and pilot builds, capture technician feedback and build lessons learned, and drive updates to documentation, tooling, processes, and training before broader production release.
  • Partner with Manufacturing Engineering, Quality Engineering, and Production Planning to ensure production‑readiness by confirming materials, tooling, fixtures, test equipment, and technician capacity, closing readiness gaps, and ensuring all work instructions, BOMs, test procedures, inspection criteria, and configuration requirements are complete and executable by production technicians.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a technical field (Engineering, Technology, Analytics); equivalent technical experience in avionics or aerospace production will be considered. 
  • 5+ years of hands‑on experience leading technicians or teams in aerospace, defense, UAS, or other advanced manufacturing settings.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly dynamic environment with evolving priorities.  
  • Excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills.  
  • U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain/maintain a security clearance 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience leading avionics or electrical assembly and integration teams within aerospace, defense, UAS, or other complex hardware manufacturing environments.
  • Proven expertise with electrical and avionics troubleshooting, system‑level diagnostics, and root‑cause analysis across wiring, electronics, sensors, power systems, and data‑interface architectures.
  • Strong proficiency reading and interpreting engineering schematics, wiring diagrams, ICDs, bills of material, work instructions, and other configuration‑controlled documentation.
  • Demonstrated success building technician capabilities, establishing production processes, and supporting early prototype through pre‑production and first‑article manufacturing.

Job Description:

 

The Senior Field Marketing Manager, Southeast Asia & Oceania will establish and execute field marketing across priority defense, government, and strategic aerospace accounts throughout Southeast Asia and Oceania. This person will drive account-based marketing programs, support strategic capture efforts, and generate measurable pipeline impact in close partnership with regional Sales, Business Development, and Capture teams.

Based in Australia and reporting to the Director of Field Marketing, Middle East / Asia, this role will have responsibility for developing and executing field marketing strategy across Australia, New Zealand, Southeast Asia, and other priority markets within the region.

This is a hands-on role in a high-growth environment. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable developing account strategies and executing field programs, thrives in complex multinational government and defense sales environments, and understands how to align marketing efforts with long-cycle defense procurement processes across diverse markets.

 

 

What you'll do:

  • Lead and execute field marketing across priority defense and government accounts in Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, and other priority Southeast Asian and Oceanian markets, tightly aligned with regional Go-to-Market priorities.
  • Develop and execute account-based marketing strategies for priority accounts, mapping buying centers and orchestrating multi-touch engagement across executive briefings, targeted campaigns, industry events, and owned customer programs.
  • Demonstrate a strong understanding of defense procurement environments, acquisition cycles, government structures, regional security frameworks, and country-specific stakeholder landscapes across Southeast Asia and Oceania.
  • Engage key ministries, agencies, and defense organizations including, but not limited to:
  • Australian Department of Defence and Australian Defence Force
  • New Zealand Ministry of Defence and New Zealand Defence Force
  • Indonesian Ministry of Defense and Indonesian Armed Forces
  • Malaysian Ministry of Defence and Malaysian Armed Forces
  • Philippine Department of National Defense and Armed Forces of the Philippines
  • Royal Thai Armed Forces and relevant Thai defense agencies
  • Vietnam Ministry of National Defence and relevant defense organizations
  • Own strategy and execution for major defense and aerospace events across the region, prioritizing high-value account engagement, customer relationships, and executive-level meetings over brand presence alone.
  • Plan and execute owned customer events, private briefings, roundtables, and targeted engagements in partnership with Sales and Capture teams to accelerate opportunity progression.
  • Align marketing programs with regional sales objectives, pipeline targets, account plans, and strategic capture priorities to drive measurable revenue impact.
  • Own Salesforce campaign execution, including creating and managing Campaign IDs, ensuring proper campaign structure, tracking member status, and maintaining data integrity in partnership with Sales.
  • Partner closely with Sales to ensure correct opportunity association, contact mapping, and required CRM field completion to support accurate pipeline reporting and attribution.
  • Build and execute programs within Marketo, including campaign flows, audience segmentation, nurture programs, performance tracking, and marketing-to-sales workflow alignment.
  • Establish KPIs aligned to regional government and defense sales realities, including account penetration, stakeholder engagement depth, opportunity influence, pipeline contribution, and deal acceleration.
  • Partner with the Director of Field Marketing, Middle East / Asia to ensure regional programs are aligned with broader Asia Pacific and Middle East field marketing strategy, priorities, processes, and best practices.
  • Share regional insights, customer intelligence, and program learnings with the broader global Field Marketing organization to strengthen Shield AI’s overall go-to-market strategy.
  • Bring structure, accountability, and operational rigor to field marketing execution across strategically important aerospace and defense markets.

Required qualifications:

  • 8 to 12 years of experience in field marketing, demand generation, or integrated marketing roles, with significant exposure to government, defense, aerospace, or national security markets across Southeast Asia and/or Oceania.
  • Demonstrated success marketing into government, military, defense, or aerospace organizations in Australia and/or other priority markets across Southeast Asia and Oceania.
  • Strong understanding of defense procurement processes, long-cycle acquisition environments, government stakeholder structures, and multi-stakeholder account development across the region.
  • Proven experience leading and executing account-based marketing programs within complex enterprise, government, or strategic accounts. ABM must be a core area of expertise.
  • Hands-on experience with Salesforce CRM, including campaign creation, Campaign ID management, opportunity alignment, required field governance, reporting, and close partnership with Sales teams on CRM hygiene and pipeline tracking.
  • Hands-on experience with Marketo, including campaign build, segmentation, nurture programs, performance tracking, and marketing-to-sales workflow alignment.
  • Experience executing trade shows, industry events, executive briefings, and owned customer programs in defense, aerospace, national security, or adjacent technology sectors.
  • Ability to engage credibly with senior military leaders, government stakeholders, defense industry executives, and technical evaluators across multiple countries and cultures.
  • Strong cross-functional partnership skills with Sales, Business Development, Capture, and Global Marketing teams.
  • Fluent in English, both written and verbal, to collaborate effectively with global teams.
  • Additional language proficiency relevant to Southeast Asia or Oceania is a plus.
  • Willingness to travel extensively across Southeast Asia and Oceania as required.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

Shield AI was founded to protect service members and civilians with intelligent systems. We are building the world’s best AI pilot and the aircraft that enable autonomy at scale. Our technology operates in complex, contested environments where GPS and communications may be denied, degraded, or unavailable.

The technology we build demands cross-functional teaming and collaborative execution to solve the hardest problems in autonomy, aerospace engineering, and robotics. Engineers at Shield AI do not work in silos — they work shoulder-to-shoulder across disciplines to rapidly move from concept to flight-ready systems deployed in the real world.  

X-BAT represents the next generation of autonomous airpower: a runway-independent, AI-piloted aircraft designed to execute missions in highly contested environments. Powered by Hivemind, Shield AI’s combat-proven autonomy stack, X-BAT combines long-range performance, survivability, and autonomous mission execution into a scalable operational platform.  

The Sr Manager of Aerostructures Design for X-BAT, role requires a technically elite aerospace leader who thrives in fast-moving environments, can build and scale high-performing engineering organizations, and is energized by solving complex problems that directly impact national security.

What you'll do:

  • Lead the aerostructures design organization for the X-BAT program.
  • Drive development of lightweight, manufacturable, survivable aircraft structures optimized for autonomous combat aircraft operations
  • Partner closely with flight sciences, propulsion, avionics, manufacturing, autonomy, flight test, and supply chain teams to deliver integrated aircraft solutions
  • Establish engineering processes, design standards, configuration management, and structural development roadmaps across the program lifecycle
  • Oversee development and validation of composite and metallic airframe structures, including primary load-bearing assemblies
  • Build and mentor a world-class aerostructures engineering team capable of rapid execution and technical excellence
  • Support transition from development programs into scalable production environments
  • Drive root-cause analysis and corrective action efforts for structural, manufacturing, and flight-test findings
  • Present technical reviews, program risks, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and external stakeholders

Required qualifications:

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Enterprise Data (R6103)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

The Sr. Manager, Enterprise Data is responsible for leading delivery across Shield AI’s Enterprise Data team as the organization enables business domains onto its governed Databricks data platform. 

This role manages the engineers and delivery work required to turn enterprise data strategy into usable, reliable data products. The Sr. Manager will establish effective delivery rhythms, guide domain prioritization, manage capacity and dependencies, and ensure that business needs are translated into clear, appropriately scoped work for the Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering, Domain Enablement, and Data Governance functions. 

The role requires substantial data and analytics depth to assess delivery approaches, challenge unclear requirements, make appropriate tradeoffs, and ensure that the team produces durable, governed, production-ready outcomes rather than one-off reporting solutions. 

The Sr. Manager partners closely with the Sr. Director of Enterprise Data & Architecture on strategy, operating model, investment priorities, executive engagement, and cross-functional alignment. The role partners with Platform Engineering and Enterprise Architecture, which remain direct functions of the Sr. Director, to ensure domain delivery is built on secure, reliable, scalable enterprise foundations. 

What you'll do:

  • Lead and develop the Enterprise Data delivery team, including Data Engineers, Analytics Engineers, Domain Enablement Engineers, and Data Governance specialists. 
  • Establish clear delivery operating rhythms for planning, prioritization, capacity management, roadmap tracking, dependency management, risk escalation, and stakeholder communication. 
  • Turn enterprise data strategy and business-domain priorities into sequenced, achievable delivery plans across platform onboarding, source integration, data-product delivery, semantic enablement, and governance. 
  • Partner with business leaders and domain stakeholders to shape intake, clarify intended outcomes, assess readiness, prioritize use cases, and establish realistic delivery expectations. 
  • Ensure domain work is appropriately scoped and sequenced, balancing near-term business value with the need for durable, governed, reusable data foundations. 
  • Coordinate delivery across Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering, Domain Enablement, and Data Governance; resolve dependencies and escalate decisions that require platform, architecture, security, infrastructure, or executive direction. 
  • Ensure team outputs meet expectations for production readiness, data quality, documentation, ownership, lineage, security, access controls, and maintainability. 
  • Review delivery plans, technical approaches, risks, and tradeoffs with technical leads; challenge work that creates unnecessary duplication, ungoverned data assets, or unsustainable operational burden. 
  • Partner with the Sr. Staff Data Engineer to align domain delivery to shared ingestion, transformation, and deployment patterns. 
  • Partner with the Staff Analytics Engineer to ensure domain assets align to enterprise semantic standards, metric definitions, and Gold-layer promotion expectations. 
  • Partner with the Platform / Data Reliability Engineer to ensure domain workloads meet platform standards for reliability, observability, cost management, environment promotion, and secure production operation. 
  • Partner with the Data Governance Specialist to ensure ownership, stewardship, classifications, metadata, lineage, quality expectations, and approvals are incorporated into delivery work. 
  • Hire, coach, develop, and retain a high-performing data team; establish role clarity, growth expectations, performance feedback, and appropriate technical leadership opportunities. 
  • Define and monitor practical measures of delivery health, including roadmap progress, throughput, time to enable new domains, adoption, quality trends, operational stability, and unresolved dependencies. 
  • Communicate delivery progress, material risks, investment needs, and tradeoffs clearly to business and technology leadership. 
  • Continuously improve the team’s delivery model as the enterprise data platform, domain portfolio, and organizational maturity evolve. 

Required qualifications:

  • 12+ years of experience across data engineering, analytics engineering, BI/data platforms, data architecture, or related technical data disciplines. 
  • 3+ years of experience leading and developing technical teams responsible for data, analytics, data products, or data-platform delivery. 
  • Demonstrated success leading delivery across multiple business domains and balancing competing stakeholder priorities. 
  • Strong understanding of modern data-platform concepts, including lakehouse architecture, data pipelines, Bronze/Silver/Gold patterns, dimensional modeling, semantic layers, data quality, metadata, lineage, and governed access. 
  • Hands-on experience with Databricks, including Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Databricks SQL, Workflows, or related lakehouse capabilities.
  • Ability to assess and challenge technical delivery approaches without needing to be the primary hands-on implementer for every solution. 
  • Experience translating business priorities into outcome-oriented roadmaps, scoped delivery plans, and realistic sequencing decisions. 
  • Experience partnering with business stakeholders, software engineering, cloud/infrastructure, security, governance, and architecture functions. 
  • Strong judgment in ambiguous, fast-moving environments with incomplete information and competing demands. 
  • Strong communication, organizational leadership, and stakeholder-management skills. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience building or scaling an enterprise data function, data-product operating model, or multi-domain analytics platform. 
  • Experience leading data delivery for Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Finance, Program Finance, GTM, HR, Engineering, or other complex enterprise domains. 
  • Experience in aerospace, defense, autonomous systems, manufacturing, government, or another regulated and security-sensitive environment. 
  • Experience leading platform migrations, modernizations, ERP transformations, or enterprise data operating-model change. 
  • Experience managing distributed, remote, partner, or blended internal/external delivery teams.

We are seeking a Senior PX Program Manager to drive the successful delivery, adoption, and continuous improvement of high-impact people initiatives across the organization. In this role, you will partner closely with PX leaders and cross-functional stakeholders to plan, coordinate, and execute complex programs that enhance organizational effectiveness, elevate the employee experience, and align with business priorities.

The ideal candidate brings strong expertise in program and project management, change management, and stakeholder engagement. You have a proven track record of driving execution in fast-paced, dynamic environments and can effectively translate strategy into action. You will play a key role in enabling PX functional leaders by developing deployment strategies, managing end-to-end project plans, driving cross-functional alignment, and ensuring organizational readiness, adoption, and long-term sustainability.

This is a full-time opportunity to advance critical PX initiatives, strengthen operational rigor, and build scalable processes that support continued organizational growth.

What You Will Do

    Program Delivery & Execution

    * Lead the planning, coordination, execution, and ongoing management of complex PX initiatives and cross-functional programs.

    * Define program scope, objectives, milestones, timelines, risks, dependencies, and success measures with PX leaders.

    * Maintain integrated program plans and operating rhythms, monitoring progress and managing risks and issues.

    * Identify and implement process improvements during project execution where there are opportunities to increase clarity, speed, or quality.

    Change Management & Adoption

    * Design and implement change management strategies that drive successful adoption, sustainability, and leader effectiveness.

    * Assess organizational impacts and readiness, and develop communication and engagement plans that support awareness and adoption.

    * Partner with leaders and subject matter experts to facilitate change and minimize disruption.

    * Track adoption and effectiveness and integrate lessons learned into future initiatives.

    Stakeholder Management & Collaboration

    * Build strong, trust-based relationships across PX functions and business teams.

    * Facilitate stakeholder alignment, decision-making, and issue resolution across multiple workstreams.

    * Coordinate cross-functional efforts to ensure cohesive program delivery and integration.

    * Provide clear, concise, executive-ready communications on program status, risks, outcomes, and recommendations.

    Governance, Reporting, and Program Development

    * Establish governance models, operating rhythms, and reporting mechanisms for strategic PX programs.

    * Develop dashboards, status reports, and executive updates that clearly convey health and progress.

    * Maintain key artifacts, including action plans, decision logs, and risk registers.

    * Optimize PX structures, standards, and workflows where there are opportunities to build more scalable, repeatable approaches.

    Required Qualifications

    * Bachelor’s degree  - preferably in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or equivalent experience.

    * 8+ years of experience leading complex programs, transformation initiatives, or organizational change efforts in an HR, PX, or related environment.

    * Demonstrated experience managing enterprise-wide, cross-functional projects with multiple stakeholders in high-growth or similarly complex environments.

    * Strong program and project management skills, including planning, governance, risk management, and execution across multiple workstreams.

    * Hands-on experience developing and implementing change management strategies, including stakeholder analysis, communications, training, and reinforcement plans.

    * Experience working directly with PX/HR/People teams on initiatives such as performance management, talent development, PX systems, or employee experience programs.

    * Ability to use quantitative and qualitative data (e.g., survey results, adoption metrics, KPIs) to inform program design, decision-making, and iteration.

    * Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and drive outcomes without direct authority.

    * Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities, with a track record of bringing structure and operating rigor to ambiguous environments.

    * Demonstrated ability to build program frameworks, playbooks, or toolkits that scale PX initiatives across multiple teams or locations.

    Preferred Qualifications

    * Experience in high-growth technology, aerospace, defense, or similarly complex environments.

    * Formal training or certification in program and/or change management (e.g., PMP, Prosci, Agile-related credentials).

    * Experience implementing or optimizing PX/HR systems and tools (e.g., HRIS, performance management, engagement or survey platforms).

  • Technical aptitude and ability to engage credibly with Engineering, Product, and Operational stakeholders

  • Self-motivated, results-oriented, and capable of operating in a fast-paced environment

Job Description:

We are seeking a detail-oriented and highly motivated Contracts Manager to join our team supporting defense simulation contracting operations. This position requires an individual with strong knowledge of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and other relevant regulations associated with defense contracts.

Job Description:

Hivemind is looking for an experienced SRE lead to help drive the establishment of our SRE function.  

As the SRE lead, you will establish and mature the reliability practices used across our cloud infrastructure and platform services. You will work with Cloud Engineering and product teams to define reliability targets, improve observability, and ensure that production systems can be operated and recovered predictably. 

This is a deeply technical, hands-on role. You will investigate complex failures, improve the systems and tooling used to operate our platforms, and turn lessons from incidents into engineering improvements. You will provide technical leadership for reliability engineering, helping teams adopt practices that improve system health without adding unnecessary process.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Job Description:

The Sr. Staff Platform / Data Reliability Engineer is responsible for making Databricks a reliable, secure, scalable, and operationally mature platform for enterprise use. This role focuses on the platform itself rather than domain-specific business modeling, ensuring the lakehouse can support multiple domains, regulated data handling, and a growing set of production workloads without becoming fragile, expensive, or hard to govern. 

This role partners closely with the Senior Staff Data Engineer, who focuses more heavily on ingestion and medallion implementation patterns, and with the existing Cloud & Infrastructure team, which owns cloud accounts, networking, and foundational infrastructure. The Platform / Data Reliability Engineer owns the Databricks operational layer that sits above that foundation: reliability, observability, deployment standards, compute and job policies, and platform enablement patterns for internal users.  

What you'll do:

  • Own operational excellence for the Databricks platform, including monitoring, alerting, observability, incident response support, and production runbook patterns for data jobs and platform services. 
  • Define and maintain CI/CD and promotion standards for Databricks assets, including workflows, jobs, notebooks, code packages, infrastructure configuration, and environment promotion from dev to prod. 
  • Design and maintain platform standards for job orchestration, cluster and compute policies, service principal usage, environment isolation, and production execution reliability.  
  • Establish reusable operational templates and enablement patterns for new domains onboarding to Databricks, including logging conventions, job tagging, metadata capture, and support handoff expectations.  
  • Partner with the Senior Data Engineer to ensure ingestion and medallion patterns are implemented in a way that is observable, recoverable, cost-aware, and secure in production. 
  • Work with the cloud/infrastructure team to align Databricks configuration and usage patterns with broader enterprise cloud standards, especially where commercial and future government-hosted environments are involved.  
  • Help enforce technical controls for data segregation, access boundaries, and operational compliance in a highly regulated environment.  
  • Track and improve platform health metrics such as job success rates, incident trends, data pipeline reliability, cost efficiency, and environment drift. 
  • Document platform standards, operational expectations, and support models so the Databricks platform can scale beyond a small founding team.  
  • Mentor internal engineers who are growing into platform responsibilities, helping expand Databricks operational knowledge within the team.  

Required qualifications:

  • 12+ years of relevant experience in data platform engineering, platform operations, site reliability engineering, or modern cloud data infrastructure.  
  • Hands-on experience with Databricks or a closely related cloud data platform in production environments. 
  • Experience designing or operating CI/CD, environment promotion, version control, and deployment automation for data platforms and pipelines.  
  • Strong understanding of platform operations concepts such as observability, monitoring, alerting, incident management, and reliability engineering.  
  • Experience with compute policy design, workload isolation, service principals, and secure production execution patterns on cloud data platforms.  
  • Ability to work effectively in a regulated or security-sensitive environment with strong expectations around access control, auditability, and operational discipline.  
  • Strong collaboration skills and comfort partnering with cloud/infrastructure, security, data engineering, and analytics stakeholders.  

Preferred qualifications:

  • Databricks certification and/or strong demonstrated expertise with Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Workflows, and Databricks Asset Bundles.  
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code and platform automation in enterprise environments.  
  • Experience supporting commercial and government or otherwise segregated environments with different compliance and access requirements.  
  • Experience in defense, aerospace, federal, or another regulated industry.

jobs.title: Sr. Staff Thermal Engineer - Aircraft Avionics & Thermal Systems (R3930)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:
Are you a passionate and innovative thermal engineer looking to help develop state of the art AI and aircraft products? Are you eager to make a positive difference in the world? Do you want to work alongside mission driven and values focused teammates?  Shield AI is just the place for you!
 
As a Sr. Staff Thermal Engineer at Shield AI, you will lead the design, analysis, and integration of aircraft avionics thermal management systems, with opportunities to flex into aircraft-level thermal and fluid systems.
 
This role is best suited for an engineer who thrives on first-principles problem solving, is comfortable with ambiguous, open-ended challenges, and can bridge technical disciplines with strong communication and collaboration skills and the ability to simplify and communicate complex problems. The engineer will be a key contributor in shaping designs, mentoring peers, and ensuring robust thermal solutions that meet mission-critical aerospace requirements.

What you'll do:

  • Contribute to thermal analysis and design efforts for unmanned aerial vehicle avionics and thermal/fluid systems.
  • Develop and validate analytical, numerical, and computational models for heat transfer and fluid flow using hand calculations and CFD tools such as FloEFD.
  • Drive test planning, instrumentation, and data analysis to correlate models with experimental results.
  • Communicate technical findings clearly through executive-level briefings, design reviews, and written reports.
  • Proactively identify risks, propose solutions, and influence electrical and/or PCBA design direction.

Required qualifications:

  • B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related discipline.
  • Minimum 7 years of professional experience in avionics or electronics thermal engineering.
  • Strong expertise in heat transfer (conduction, convection, radiation) and fluid mechanics.
  • Deep understanding of active and passive cooling solutions and their integration at component and system level.
  • Deep understanding of thermal management design elements including TIMs, spreaders, heat sinks, vapor chambers, heat pipes, and fans
  • Proficiency with thermal analysis and CFD tools (e.g., ANSYS Icepak, FloEFD, STAR-CCM+).
  • Proficiency with CAD design tools such as NX, SolidWorks, or similar.
  • Demonstrated experience applying first-principles reasoning to complex engineering problems.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of leading technical discussions and presenting to stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to learn and adapt quickly to new tools, processes, and technical challenges in a fast paced, startup environment.
  • Ability to obtain a S//SAR level security clearance desired.

Preferred qualifications:

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in a relevant engineering discipline.
  • Experience with high altitude aircraft avionics cooling and thermal design.
  • Familiarity with aircraft integration constraints (power, weight, volume, maintainability, safety).
  • Hands-on experience with thermal and fluid system testing, instrumentation, and validation.
  • Knowledge of materials and manufacturing methods relevant to thermal management (pumps, heat exchangers, composites, etc.)
  • Experience guiding trade studies, proposals, and customer interactions in aerospace or defense programs.
  • Background in multi-disciplinary system integration, spanning avionics, fluid systems, and systems engineering

jobs.title: Sr. Supervisor, Facilities Operations, U.S. Central (R6095)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Senior Supervisor, Facilities to lead safe, reliable, and consistent Facilities Operations across an assigned region. This role directly supervises Facilities Coordinators, manages regional service delivery, leads qualifying non-capital facilities projects, and serves as the primary Facilities partner to site and business leadership. 

This is a hands-on people-leadership role. The successful candidate will move comfortably between coaching employees, resolving urgent facility issues, coordinating vendors, managing budgets and commitments, leading workplace improvements, communicating with employees, and using operating data to improve performance. 

The Senior Supervisor executes within global and regional standards while applying sound judgment to local conditions. The role is accountable for regional implementation and escalation; enterprise strategy, policy, and major capital delivery remain with the appropriate functional owners

What you'll do:

    Lead and Develop the Regional Facilities Team 
  • Directly supervise, coach, and develop Facilities Coordinators assigned to the region. 
  • Set priorities, clarify ownership, delegate work, and establish consistent expectations for service, responsiveness, documentation, and follow-through. 
  • Conduct regular team meetings, one-on-ones, performance feedback, development planning, and workload reviews in partnership with People Experience. 
  • Build cross-site coverage plans, balance workload, and maintain continuity during absences, business events, incidents, and periods of rapid growth. 
  • Create a culture of ownership, proactive communication, customer service, safety, and continuous improvement. 
  • Identify skill, capacity, and succession needs and elevate them through the applicable Facilities Operations leader. 
    • Operate the Regional Portfolio 
  • Lead day-to-day Facilities Operations across offices, engineering spaces, manufacturing environments, laboratories, hangars, warehouses, and secure or classified areas, as applicable. 
  • Maintain safe, professional, operationally ready workplaces that support employee productivity and business continuity. 
  • Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance, work orders, building services, utilities, landlord obligations, and service-provider response. 
  • Serve as the regional Facilities escalation point for outages, service failures, workplace issues, and operational risks. 
  • Implement global and regional standards, standard operating procedures, service levels, and documentation practices across assigned locations. 
  • Coordinate with landlords, property managers, technicians, vendors, and internal partners to resolve recurring issues and reduce operational disruption. 
  • Support occupancy changes, employee moves, visitor readiness, meetings, events, and other workplace-service needs within the approved service model. 
    • Lead Non-Capital Facilities Projects and Support Major Project Turnover 
  • Plan and deliver regional facilities projects that fall below Capital Delivery thresholds or do not require dedicated capital-project ownership. 
  • Lead qualifying work such as minor improvements, space reconfigurations, restacks, furniture deployments, moves/adds/changes, signage, small repairs, workplace refreshes, service rollouts, landlord-coordinated work, and lifecycle replacements within delegated authority. 
  • Define scope, coordinate stakeholders and vendors, manage schedule and cost, maintain documentation, communicate impacts, and close out assigned operational projects. 
  • For major capital projects, provide site requirements, maintainability input, local coordination, shutdown planning, employee communications, readiness support, and operational acceptance. 
  • Participate in commissioning and formal turnover to verify required training, warranties, asset records, spare parts, documentation, and operating procedures are complete. 
  • Escalate work that exceeds approved cost, risk, technical-complexity, or governance thresholds to Capital Delivery and Facilities Operations leadership. 
    • Manage Vendors, Service Partners, and Regional Financial Execution 
  • Direct and coordinate regional vendors, contractors, landlord teams, technicians, and outsourced service providers. 
  • Monitor service quality, responsiveness, safety, scope compliance, cost, and performance against approved contracts and service expectations. 
  • Review invoices, track purchase orders and commitments, support monthly forecasts, and maintain accurate budget and project documentation. 
  • Identify cost risks, service gaps, and opportunities to improve value without compromising safety, reliability, compliance, or employee experience. 
  • Support sourcing, onboarding, renewals, and performance reviews in partnership with Procurement and the applicable Facilities Operations leader. 
    • Implement EH&S, Security, and Compliance Requirements 
  • Partner with Global EH&S to implement workplace-safety, environmental, industrial-hygiene, contractor-safety, emergency-preparedness, and corrective-action requirements. 
  • Partner with Security to implement physical-security, access-control, visitor, incident-response, and secure-facility operating requirements within the approved scope. 
  • Confirm contractors and vendors meet site access, safety, security, insurance, and work-control requirements before and during execution. 
  • Support inspections, audits, emergency exercises, incident reviews, and timely closure of assigned corrective actions. 
  • Escalate material safety, security, environmental, regulatory, service, and business-continuity risks promptly and clearly. 
  • Coordinate with IT, People, Capital Delivery, Global Real Estate, Finance, Procurement, and business leadership as regional needs require. 
    • Deliver a Consistent Employee and Customer Experience 
  • Serve as the principal regional Facilities contact for site leaders, employees, and business partners. 
  • Communicate planned outages, construction impacts, relocations, service changes, and restoration activities clearly and proactively. 
  • Resolve recurring service issues, gather feedback, and balance customer needs with standards, risk, budget, and portfolio priorities. 
  • Build trusted relationships with local leadership while maintaining consistent enterprise practices across sites. 
    • Use Data, Governance, and Continuous Improvement to Raise Performance 
  • Maintain accurate regional reporting for work orders, maintenance, vendors, budget, projects, incidents, risks, actions, and customer experience. 
  • Participate in recurring Facilities Operations reviews and other governance forums, presenting issues, trends, decisions, and corrective actions. 
  • Maintain regional risk, issue, and action registers and drive assigned items to timely closure. 
  • Use operating data and root-cause analysis to improve reliability, workflows, standards, documentation, and service quality. 
  • Share lessons learned and effective practices across regions and maintain accurate information in approved Facilities systems. 

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in facilities, business, operations, engineering, construction, communications, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. 
  • 3+ years of progressive experience across facilities, workplace, office operations, property operations, project coordination, vendor management, or a closely related operating function. 
  • Demonstrated leadership of people, projects, vendors, or cross-functional teams through direct supervision, work direction, training, mentoring, project leadership, meeting leadership, or comparable responsibility. 
  • Experience supporting multiple sites, a complex campus, or multiple concurrent operational workstreams with competing priorities. 
  • Demonstrated ability to plan and deliver workplace improvements, moves, service rollouts, minor facility projects, or related operational initiatives. 
  • Experience coordinating vendors or contractors and managing scopes, schedules, service expectations, purchase orders, invoices, or budget documentation. 
  • Working knowledge of facility operations and commercial building services, with the ability to learn and apply requirements involving HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire and life safety, access control, and other building systems. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to work effectively with employees, technical partners, vendors, and senior site stakeholders. 
  • Ability to use work-management, project, collaboration, and reporting tools to maintain accurate records and communicate performance. 
  • Ability to work primarily on-site, travel throughout the assigned region, and support planned or unplanned after-hours response when required. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Prior experience directly supervising employees or leading a distributed site-services team. 
  • Experience in aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, engineering, technology, laboratory, aviation, or another mission-critical environment. 
  • Experience supporting secure, controlled-access, or classified facilities; ICD 705 familiarity or training is a plus. 
  • Experience with a computerized maintenance management system, integrated workplace management system, building management system, or comparable facilities platform. 
  • Experience supporting facility openings, expansions, relocations, construction coordination, commissioning, or operational turnover. 
  • Familiarity with OSHA requirements, contractor-safety practices, emergency response, and corrective-action management. 
  • CFM, FMP, SFP, OSHA 30, LEED, project-management, or another relevant professional credential. 

Leadership expectations:

  • Lead from the front while building the capability and confidence of the regional team. 
  • Own regional outcomes and create clarity around priorities, decisions, and follow-through. 
  • Operate through standards and data rather than relying solely on relationships or institutional knowledge. 
  • Communicate early, surface risks without delay, and avoid surprises. 
  • Exercise judgment within delegated authority and escalate issues requiring functional or executive decisions. 
  • Partner effectively across Facilities Operations, Capital Delivery, Global Real Estate, EH&S, Security, IT, People, Finance, Procurement, and the business. 

Work environment, travel, and availability:

  • This role is primarily on-site and supports facilities throughout the assigned region. 
  • Regional travel is expected at approximately 20%, with frequency adjusted for site needs, projects, incidents, and team development. 
  • The role may operate in office, engineering, manufacturing, warehouse, hangar, laboratory, construction-adjacent, or secure environments, as applicable. 
  • Availability for occasional early-morning, evening, weekend, or on-call response is required when critical facility conditions or business needs arise.

jobs.title: Sr. Supervisor, Facilities Operations, U.S. West (R6106)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Senior Supervisor, Facilities to lead safe, reliable, and consistent Facilities Operations across an assigned region. This role directly supervises Facilities Coordinators, manages regional service delivery, leads qualifying non-capital facilities projects, and serves as the primary Facilities partner to site and business leadership. 

This is a hands-on people-leadership role. The successful candidate will move comfortably between coaching employees, resolving urgent facility issues, coordinating vendors, managing budgets and commitments, leading workplace improvements, communicating with employees, and using operating data to improve performance. 

The Senior Supervisor executes within global and regional standards while applying sound judgment to local conditions. The role is accountable for regional implementation and escalation; enterprise strategy, policy, and major capital delivery remain with the appropriate functional owners. 

What you'll do:

    Lead and Develop the Regional Facilities Team 
  • Directly supervise, coach, and develop Facilities Coordinators assigned to the region. 
  • Set priorities, clarify ownership, delegate work, and establish consistent expectations for service, responsiveness, documentation, and follow-through. 
  • Conduct regular team meetings, one-on-ones, performance feedback, development planning, and workload reviews in partnership with People Experience. 
  • Build cross-site coverage plans, balance workload, and maintain continuity during absences, business events, incidents, and periods of rapid growth. 
  • Create a culture of ownership, proactive communication, customer service, safety, and continuous improvement. 
  • Identify skill, capacity, and succession needs and elevate them through the applicable Facilities Operations leader. 
    • Operate the Regional Portfolio 
  • Lead day-to-day Facilities Operations across offices, engineering spaces, manufacturing environments, laboratories, hangars, warehouses, and secure or classified areas, as applicable. 
  • Maintain safe, professional, operationally ready workplaces that support employee productivity and business continuity. 
  • Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance, work orders, building services, utilities, landlord obligations, and service-provider response. 
  • Serve as the regional Facilities escalation point for outages, service failures, workplace issues, and operational risks. 
  • Implement global and regional standards, standard operating procedures, service levels, and documentation practices across assigned locations. 
  • Coordinate with landlords, property managers, technicians, vendors, and internal partners to resolve recurring issues and reduce operational disruption. 
  • Support occupancy changes, employee moves, visitor readiness, meetings, events, and other workplace-service needs within the approved service model. 
    • Lead Non-Capital Facilities Projects and Support Major Project Turnover 
  • Plan and deliver regional facilities projects that fall below Capital Delivery thresholds or do not require dedicated capital-project ownership. 
  • Lead qualifying work such as minor improvements, space reconfigurations, restacks, furniture deployments, moves/adds/changes, signage, small repairs, workplace refreshes, service rollouts, landlord-coordinated work, and lifecycle replacements within delegated authority. 
  • Define scope, coordinate stakeholders and vendors, manage schedule and cost, maintain documentation, communicate impacts, and close out assigned operational projects. 
  • For major capital projects, provide site requirements, maintainability input, local coordination, shutdown planning, employee communications, readiness support, and operational acceptance. 
  • Participate in commissioning and formal turnover to verify required training, warranties, asset records, spare parts, documentation, and operating procedures are complete. 
  • Escalate work that exceeds approved cost, risk, technical-complexity, or governance thresholds to Capital Delivery and Facilities Operations leadership. 
    • Manage Vendors, Service Partners, and Regional Financial Execution 
  • Direct and coordinate regional vendors, contractors, landlord teams, technicians, and outsourced service providers. 
  • Monitor service quality, responsiveness, safety, scope compliance, cost, and performance against approved contracts and service expectations. 
  • Review invoices, track purchase orders and commitments, support monthly forecasts, and maintain accurate budget and project documentation. 
  • Identify cost risks, service gaps, and opportunities to improve value without compromising safety, reliability, compliance, or employee experience. 
  • Support sourcing, onboarding, renewals, and performance reviews in partnership with Procurement and the applicable Facilities Operations leader. 
    • Implement EH&S, Security, and Compliance Requirements 
  • Partner with Global EH&S to implement workplace-safety, environmental, industrial-hygiene, contractor-safety, emergency-preparedness, and corrective-action requirements. 
  • Partner with Security to implement physical-security, access-control, visitor, incident-response, and secure-facility operating requirements within the approved scope. 
  • Confirm contractors and vendors meet site access, safety, security, insurance, and work-control requirements before and during execution. 
  • Support inspections, audits, emergency exercises, incident reviews, and timely closure of assigned corrective actions. 
  • Escalate material safety, security, environmental, regulatory, service, and business-continuity risks promptly and clearly. 
  • Coordinate with IT, People, Capital Delivery, Global Real Estate, Finance, Procurement, and business leadership as regional needs require. 
    • Deliver a Consistent Employee and Customer Experience 
  • Serve as the principal regional Facilities contact for site leaders, employees, and business partners. 
  • Communicate planned outages, construction impacts, relocations, service changes, and restoration activities clearly and proactively. 
  • Resolve recurring service issues, gather feedback, and balance customer needs with standards, risk, budget, and portfolio priorities. 
  • Build trusted relationships with local leadership while maintaining consistent enterprise practices across sites. 
    • Use Data, Governance, and Continuous Improvement to Raise Performance 
  • Maintain accurate regional reporting for work orders, maintenance, vendors, budget, projects, incidents, risks, actions, and customer experience. 
  • Participate in recurring Facilities Operations reviews and other governance forums, presenting issues, trends, decisions, and corrective actions. 
  • Maintain regional risk, issue, and action registers and drive assigned items to timely closure. 
  • Use operating data and root-cause analysis to improve reliability, workflows, standards, documentation, and service quality. 
  • Share lessons learned and effective practices across regions and maintain accurate information in approved Facilities systems. 

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in facilities, business, operations, engineering, construction, communications, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. 
  • 3+ years of progressive experience across facilities, workplace, office operations, property operations, project coordination, vendor management, or a closely related operating function. 
  • Demonstrated leadership of people, projects, vendors, or cross-functional teams through direct supervision, work direction, training, mentoring, project leadership, meeting leadership, or comparable responsibility. 
  • Experience supporting multiple sites, a complex campus, or multiple concurrent operational workstreams with competing priorities. 
  • Demonstrated ability to plan and deliver workplace improvements, moves, service rollouts, minor facility projects, or related operational initiatives. 
  • Experience coordinating vendors or contractors and managing scopes, schedules, service expectations, purchase orders, invoices, or budget documentation. 
  • Working knowledge of facility operations and commercial building services, with the ability to learn and apply requirements involving HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire and life safety, access control, and other building systems. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound judgment, and the ability to work effectively with employees, technical partners, vendors, and senior site stakeholders. 
  • Ability to use work-management, project, collaboration, and reporting tools to maintain accurate records and communicate performance. 
  • Ability to work primarily on-site, travel throughout the assigned region, and support planned or unplanned after-hours response when required. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Prior experience directly supervising employees or leading a distributed site-services team. 
  • Experience in aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, engineering, technology, laboratory, aviation, or another mission-critical environment. 
  • Experience supporting secure, controlled-access, or classified facilities; ICD 705 familiarity or training is a plus.
  • Experience with a computerized maintenance management system, integrated workplace management system, building management system, or comparable facilities platform. 
  • Experience supporting facility openings, expansions, relocations, construction coordination, commissioning, or operational turnover. 
  • Familiarity with OSHA requirements, contractor-safety practices, emergency response, and corrective-action management. 
  • CFM, FMP, SFP, OSHA 30, LEED, project-management, or another relevant professional credential. 

Leadership expectations:

  • Lead from the front while building the capability and confidence of the regional team. 
  • Own regional outcomes and create clarity around priorities, decisions, and follow-through. 
  • Operate through standards and data rather than relying solely on relationships or institutional knowledge. 
  • Communicate early, surface risks without delay, and avoid surprises. 
  • Exercise judgment within delegated authority and escalate issues requiring functional or executive decisions. 
  • Partner effectively across Facilities Operations, Capital Delivery, Global Real Estate, EH&S, Security, IT, People, Finance, Procurement, and the business. 

Work environment, travel, and availability:

  • This role is primarily on-site and supports facilities throughout the assigned region. 
  • Regional travel is expected at approximately 20%, with frequency adjusted for site needs, projects, incidents, and team development.
  • The role may operate in office, engineering, manufacturing, warehouse, hangar, laboratory, construction-adjacent, or secure environments, as applicable. 
  • Availability for occasional early-morning, evening, weekend, or on-call response is required when critical facility conditions or business needs arise.
